Makes the player spectate the entity.

To get the applied spectated entity, use [Player:GetObserverTarget](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:GetObserverTarget).

args.name: entity
args.description: Entity to spectate.

entries.name: SprayDecal
entries.description: Makes a player spray their decal.

args.name: sprayOrigin
args.description: The location to spray from

args.name: sprayEndPos
args.description: The location to spray to

entries.name: SprintDisable
entries.description: Disables the sprint on the player.

entries.name: SprintEnable
entries.description: Enables the sprint on the player.

entries.name: StartMove
entries.description:
Called from [GM:CreateMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:CreateMove).

**WARNING**: This hook will not work if the current gamemode overrides [GM:SetupMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:SetupMove) and does not call this hook.


**NOTE**: This hook is run after the [drive.StartMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/drive.StartMove) has been called.

args.name: mv
args.description: The move data to override/use

args.name: cmd
args.description: The command data

returns.description: Return true to prevent default action

entries.name: StartSprinting
entries.description: Doesn't appear to do anything.
entries.deprecated: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

entries.name: StartWalking
entries.description: When used in a [GM:SetupMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function will force the player to walk, as well as preventing the player from sprinting.
entries.deprecated: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

entries.name: SteamID
entries.description:
Returns the player's SteamID.

See [Player:AccountID](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:AccountID) for a shorter version of the SteamID and [Player:SteamID64](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SteamID64) for the full SteamID.

It is recommended to use [Player:SteamID64](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SteamID64) over the other SteamID formats whenever possible.

**NOTE**: In a `-multirun` environment, this will return `STEAM_ID_LAN` for all "copies" of a player because they are not authenticated with Steam.

For Bots this will return `BOT`.

returns.description: "Text" representation of the player's SteamID.

entries.name: SteamID64
entries.description:
Returns the player's full **64-bit SteamID**, also known as **CommunityID**. Information on how data is packed into this value can be found [here](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamID).

See [Player:AccountID](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:AccountID) for a function that returns only the Account ID part of the SteamID and [Player:SteamID](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SteamID) for the text version of the SteamID.

**NOTE**: In a `-multirun` environment, this will return `"0"` for all "copies" of a player because they are not authenticated with Steam.

For bots, this will return `90071996842377216` (equivalent to `STEAM_0:0:0`) for the first bot to join.

For each additional bot, the number increases by 1. So the next bot will be `90071996842377217` (`STEAM_0:1:0`) then `90071996842377218` (`STEAM_0:0:1`) and so on.

returns.description:
Player's 64-bit SteamID aka CommunityID.

The return value is a string, not a number, since Lua's numbers are unable to store the entire 64bit numbers without data loss.

entries.name: StopSprinting
entries.description:
When used in a [GM:SetupMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function will prevent the player from sprinting.

When +walk is engaged, the player will still be able to sprint to half speed (normal run speed) as opposed to full sprint speed without this function.
entries.deprecated: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

entries.name: StopWalking
entries.description: When used in a [GM:SetupMove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function behaves unexpectedly by preventing the player from sprinting similar to [Player:StopSprinting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:StopSprinting).
entries.deprecated: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

entries.name: StopZooming
entries.description:
Turns off the zoom mode of the player. (+zoom console command)

Basically equivalent of entering "-zoom" into player's console.

entries.name: StripAmmo
entries.description: Removes all ammo from the player.
entries.deprecated: Alias of Player:RemoveAllAmmo

entries.name: StripWeapon
entries.description:
Removes the specified weapon class from a certain player  
	**NOTE**: this function will call the [Entity:OnRemove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:OnRemove) but if you try use [Entity:GetOwner](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetOwner) it will return nil

args.name: weapon
args.description: The weapon class to remove

entries.name: StripWeapons
entries.description: Removes all weapons from a certain player

entries.name: SuppressHint

Prevents a hint from showing up.


**NOTE**: This function is only available in Sandbox and its derivatives

args.name: name
args.description: Hint name/class/index to prevent from showing up. You can find a list of hint names for this function List_of_Hint_Classes.

entries.name: SwitchToDefaultWeapon
entries.description:
Attempts to switch the player weapon to the one specified in the "cl_defaultweapon" convar, if the player does not own the specified weapon nothing will happen.

If you want to switch to a specific weapon, use: [Player:SetActiveWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SetActiveWeapon)

entries.name: Team
entries.description:
Returns the player's team ID, set by [Player:SetTeam](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SetTeam)

Returns 0 clientside when the game is not fully loaded.

returns.description: The player's team's index number, as in the Enums/TEAM or a custom team defined in team.SetUp.

entries.name: TimeConnected
entries.description:
Returns the time in seconds since the player connected.

Bots will always return value 0.

returns.name: connectedTime
returns.description: How long this player was connected to the server for, in seconds.

entries.name: TraceHullAttack
entries.description:
Performs a trace hull and applies damage to the entities hit, returns the first entity hit.

**WARNING**: Hitting the victim entity with this function in [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage) can cause infinite loops.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The start position of the hull trace.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The end position of the hull trace.

args.name: mins
args.description: The minimum coordinates of the hull.

args.name: maxs
args.description: The maximum coordinates of the hull.

args.name: damage
args.description: The damage to be applied.

args.name: damageFlags
args.description: Bitflag specifying the damage type, see Enums/DMG.

args.name: damageForce
args.description: The force to be applied to the hit object.

args.name: damageAllNPCs
args.description: Whether to apply damage to all hit NPCs or not.

returns.description: The hit entity

entries.name: TranslateWeaponActivity
entries.description: Translates [Enums/ACT](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/ACT) according to the holdtype of players currently held weapon.

args.name: act
args.description: The initial Enums/ACT

returns.description: Translated Enums/ACT

entries.name: UnfreezePhysicsObjects
entries.description: Unfreezes all objects the player has frozen with their Physics Gun. Same as double pressing R while holding Physics Gun.

entries.name: UniqueID
entries.description:
Returns a 32 bit integer that remains constant for a player across joins/leaves and across different servers. This can be used when a string is inappropriate - e.g. in a database primary key.



**NOTE**: In Singleplayer, this function will always return 1.

In a `-multirun` environment, the value returned is different on the serverside and clientside.

returns.description: The player's Unique ID

entries.deprecated: **This function has collisions,** where more than one player can have the same UniqueID. It is **highly** recommended to use Player:SteamID64, Player:SteamID or Player:AccountID instead, which are guaranteed to be unique to each player.

entries.name: UniqueIDTable
entries.description:
Returns a table that will stay allocated for the specific player serverside between connects until the server shuts down or change map. On client it has no such special behavior.

**NOTE**: This table is not synchronized (networked) between client and server.

args.name: key
args.description: Unique table key.

returns.description: The table that contains any info you have put in it.

entries.name: UnLock
entries.description:
Unlocks the player movement if locked previously.

Will disable godmode for the player if locked previously.

entries.name: UnSpectate
entries.description:
Removes the player from the spectate mode entirely.

The player must be respawned, otherwise they will be able to walk through doors and become invincible. This will be fixed in a future update.

entries.name: UserID
entries.description:

You can use [Global.Player](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Player) global function to get a player by their user ID.

entries.name: CreateNextBot
entries.description:
Similar to the serverside command "bot", this function creates a new Player bot with the given name. This bot will not obey to the usual `bot_*` commands, and it's the same bot base used in TF2 and CS:S.

The best way to control the behaviour of a Player bot right now is to use the [GM:StartCommand](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:StartCommand) hook and modify its input serverside.

**NOTE**: Despite this Player being fake, it has to be removed from the server by using [Player:Kick](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:Kick) and **NOT** [Entity:Remove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:Remove).
Also keep in mind that these bots still use player slots, so you won't be able to spawn them in singleplayer!


**NOTE**: Any Bot created using this method will be considered UnAuthed by Garry's Mod

args.description:
The name of the bot, using an already existing name will append brackets at the end of it with a number pertaining it.

Example: "Bot name test", "Bot name test(1)".

entries.name: Iterator
entries.description:
Returns a [Stateless Iterator](https://www.lua.org/pil/7.3.html) for all players on the server.
		Intended for use in [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).  
		See [ents.Iterator](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ents.Iterator) for a similar function for all entities.

		**NOTE**: Internally, this function uses cached values that are stored in Lua, as opposed to [player.GetAll](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/player.GetAll), which is a C++ function.
		Because a call operation from Lua to C++ *and* with a return back to Lua is quite costly, this function will be more efficient than [player.GetAll](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/player.GetAll).

returns.description: The Iterator Function from Global.ipairs.

Table of all existing Player.  This is a cached copy of player.GetAll.
This table is intended to be read-only.

Modifying the return table will affect all subsequent calls to this function until the cache is refreshed, replacing all of your player.GetAll usages may come with unintended side effects because of this.

An example:
```
-- Bad code.
local scan_ents = select( 2, player.Iterator() )
table.Add( scan_ents, ents.FindByClass( "ttt_decoy" ) )

-- Fine code. A copy of the table is being made and used.
local scan_ents = table.Copy( select( 2, player.Iterator() ) )
table.Add( scan_ents, ents.FindByClass( "ttt_decoy" ) )
```

The starting index for the table of players.  
			This is always `0` and is returned for the benefit of [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).

entries.name: PolygonVertex
entries.description:
A structure containing vertex information for use with [surface.DrawPoly](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/surface.DrawPoly).

UV coordinates describe which part of a given texture should be drawn at a vertex - your graphics card's interpolator will fill in space between vertices. UV coords range from `0-1`, with `0` being top/left and `1` being bottom/right. If you're using a texture these are mandatory.

**NOTE**: You must pass a table of tables with this structure to the function. **You need to pass at least 3 points.**

Your points must be defined in a **clockwise order.** Otherwise, your shape will not render properly.

fields.description: The x coordinate of the vertex.

fields.name: u
fields.description: The u texture coordinate of the vertex. `Can be left blank.`

fields.name: v

entries.name: SetAngles
entries.description:
Sets the angles (direction) of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetBrightness
entries.description:
Sets the brightness of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: brightness
args.description: The brightness to give the projected texture. A float from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100% brightness. Can be higher.

entries.name: SetColor
entries.description:
Sets the color of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: color
args.description: Unlike other projected textures, this color can only go up to 255.

entries.name: SetConstantAttenuation
entries.description:
Sets the constant attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetEnableShadows
entries.description:
Enable or disable shadows cast from the projected texture.

**NOTE**: As with all types of projected textures (including the player's flashlight and env_projectedtexture), there can only be 8 projected textures with shadows enabled in total.This limit can be increased with the launch parameter `-numshadowtextures LIMIT` where `LIMIT` is the new limit.Naturally, many projected lights with shadows enabled will drastically decrease framerate.


You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetFarZ
entries.description:
Sets the distance at which the projected texture ends.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetFOV
entries.description:
Sets the angle of projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: fov
args.description: Must be higher than 0 and lower than 180

entries.name: SetHorizontalFOV
entries.description:
Sets the horizontal angle of projection without affecting the vertical angle.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: hFOV
args.description: The new horizontal Field Of View for the projected texture. Must be in range between 0 and 180.

entries.name: SetLightWorld
entries.description: Set whenever or not the Texture should light up world geometry.

args.name: lightworld
args.description: Set it to `true` if the Texture should light up world geometry.

entries.name: SetLinearAttenuation
entries.description:
Sets the linear attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation).

The default value of linear attenuation when the projected texture is created is 100. (others are 0, as you are not supposed to mix them)

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetNearZ
entries.description:
Sets the distance at which the projected texture begins its projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

**NOTE**: Setting this to 0 will disable the projected texture completely! This may be useful if you want to disable a projected texture without actually removing it


**NOTE**: This seems to affect the rendering of shadows - a higher Near Z value will have shadows begin to render closer to their casting object. Comparing a low Near Z value (like 1) with a normal one (12) or high one (1000) is the easiest way to understand this artifact

entries.name: SetNoCull
entries.description:
Allows disabling of projected texture view-frustum culling for cases where said culling creates unwanted side effects. Disabling culling will have a negative effect on performance.

Culling makes projected textures off screen to stop rendering/updating.

args.name: enable
args.description: `false` to enable culling (default), `true` to disable.

entries.name: SetOrthographic
entries.description:
Changes the current projected texture between orthographic and perspective projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

Shadows dont work. (For non static props and for most map brushes)

args.name: orthographic
args.description: When false, all other arguments are ignored and the texture is reset to perspective projection.

args.name: left
args.description: The amount of units left from the projected texture's origin to project.

args.name: top
args.description: The amount of units upwards from the projected texture's origin to project.

args.name: right
args.description: The amount of units right from the projected texture's origin to project.

args.name: bottom
args.description: The amount of units downwards from the projected texture's origin to project.

entries.name: SetPos
entries.description:
Move the Projected Texture to the specified position.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetQuadraticAttenuation
entries.description:
Sets the quadratic attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

entries.name: SetShadowDepthBias
entries.description:
Sets the shadow depth bias of the projected texture.

The initial value is `0.0001`. Normal projected textures obey the value of the `mat_depthbias_shadowmap` [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: bias
args.description: The shadow depth bias to set.

entries.name: SetShadowFilter
entries.description:
Sets the shadow "filter size" of the projected texture. `0` is fully pixelated, higher values will blur the shadow more. The initial value is the value of `r_projectedtexture_filter` [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: filter
args.description: The shadow filter size to set.

entries.name: SetShadowSlopeScaleDepthBias
entries.description:
Sets the shadow depth slope scale bias of the projected texture.

The initial value is `2`. Normal projected textures obey the value of the `mat_slopescaledepthbias_shadowmap` [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: bias
args.description: The shadow depth slope scale bias to set.

entries.name: SetSkipShadowUpdates
entries.description: Sets whether shadow updates are disabled for this ProjectedTexture. This can be useful to save up on performance, but it will inevitably cause graphical glitches if left not updating for long.

args.name: enable
args.description: Whether future shadow updates should be skipped.

entries.name: SetTargetEntity
entries.description:
Sets the target entity for this projected texture, meaning it will only be lighting the given entity and the world.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: target
args.description: The target entity, or `NULL` to reset.

entries.name: SetTexture
entries.description:
Sets the texture to be projected.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: texture
args.description: The name of the texture. Can also be an ITexture.

entries.name: SetTextureFrame
entries.description:
For animated textures, this will choose which frame in the animation will be projected.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: frame
args.description: The frame index to use.

entries.name: SetVerticalFOV
entries.description:
Sets the vertical angle of projection without affecting the horizontal angle.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

args.name: vFOV
args.description: The new vertical Field Of View for the projected texture. Must be in range between 0 and 180.

entries.name: Update
entries.description:
Updates the Projected Light and applies all previously set parameters.

The best place to call this function is in [GM:PreDrawOpaqueRenderables](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PreDrawOpaqueRenderables).

entries.name: properties
entries.description: The properties library gives you access to the menu that shows up when right clicking entities while holding C.

entries.name: Add
entries.description: Add properties to the properties module. Properties can be blocked via [GM:CanProperty](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:CanProperty).

args.name: name
args.description: A unique name used to identify the property

args.name: propertyData
args.description: A table that defines the property. Uses the Structures/PropertyAdd.

entries.name: CanBeTargeted
entries.description:
Returns true if given entity can be targeted by the player via the properties system.

This should be used serverside in your properties to prevent abuse by clientside scripting.

args.name: ent
args.description: The entity to test

args.name: ply
args.description: If given, will also perform a distance check based on the entity's Orientated Bounding Box.

returns.description: True if entity can be targeted, false otherwise

entries.name: GetHovered
entries.description: Returns an entity player is hovering over with their cursor.

args.name: pos
args.description: Eye position of local player, Entity:EyePos

args.name: aimVec
args.description: Aim vector of local player, Player:GetAimVector

returns.description: The hovered entity

entries.name: OnScreenClick
entries.description: Checks if player hovers over any entities and open a properties menu for it.

args.name: eyepos
args.description: The eye pos of a player

args.name: eyevec
args.description: The aim vector of a player

entries.name: OpenEntityMenu
entries.description: Opens properties menu for given entity.

args.name: ent
args.description: The entity to open menu for

args.name: tr
args.description: The trace that is passed as second argument to Action callback of a property

entries.name: Remove
entries.description: Remove an entity right-click property. See [properties.Add](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/properties.Add) for details.

args.name: name
args.description: A unique name used to identify the property to be removed.

entries.name: PropertyAdd
entries.description: Structure used for [properties.Add](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/properties.Add).

fields.name: Type
fields.description: Can be set to "toggle" to make this property a toggle property.

fields.name: MenuLabel
fields.description: Label to show on opened menu

fields.name: MenuIcon
fields.description: Icon to show on opened menu for this item. Optional for simple properties and unused for toggle properties.

fields.name: Order
fields.description:
Where in the list should the property be positioned, relative to other properties.

For reference, here are the default properties and their Order values:

Property |  Order |
---------|-------|
| Bone Manipulate | 500 |
| Bodygroups | 600 |
| Skin | 601 |
| Keep Upright | 900 |
| Ignite/Extinguish | 999 |
| Remove | 1000 |
| Gravity | 1001 |
| Drive | 1100 |
| Collision | 1500 |
| Statue | 1501 |
| NPC Biggify/Smallify | 1799, 1800 |
| Motion Control (Kinect) | 2500 |
| Editable_Entities | 90001 |

fields.name: PrependSpacer
fields.description: Whether to add a spacer before this property. This should generally be true for the first property in a group of properties.

fields.name: Filter
fields.description:
Used **clientside** to decide whether this property should be shown for an entity.

It's good practice to call GM:CanProperty in this hook via gamemode.Call or hook.Run.



Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* Entity `ent` - the entity the player clicked
* Player `player` - the Global.LocalPlayer

Function return value(s):
* boolean `check` - Return true if the property should be shown for this entity.

returns.name: check
returns.description: Return true if the property should be shown for this entity.

fields.name: Checked
fields.description:
Required for toggle properties (clientside).



Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* Entity `ent` - the entity the player clicked
* table `tr` - the player's eye trace

Function return value(s):
* boolean `check` - Return true if the property should appear checked in the UI.

returns.name: check
returns.description: Return true if the property should appear checked in the UI.

fields.name: Action
fields.description:
Called **clientside** when the property is clicked


Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* Entity `ent` - the entity the player clicked
* table `tr` - the player's eye trace


When appropriate, within this function you can call `self:MsgStart()`, write data with the net.`Write*` functions, and finish with `self:MsgEnd()`. This will activate the `Receive` function on the server. In most cases, you will want to send the entity to the server, as it's not done by default.

fields.name: Receive
fields.description:
Called **serverside** if the client sends a message in the `Action` function (see above).



Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* number `len` - the net message length, although this includes the property identifier used internally (the name of the property)
* Player `ply` - the player who clicked the property


You can read data received from the client with the net.`Read*` functions. It's good practice to check GM:CanProperty here via gamemode.Call or hook.Run.

arguments.name: len
arguments.description: the net message length, although this includes the property identifier used internally (the name of the property)

arguments.name: ply
arguments.description: the player who clicked the property

fields.name: MenuOpen
fields.description:
Called **clientside** when the property option has been created in the right-click menu. This is not called for toggle properties!


Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* DMenuOption `option` - the menu option
* Entity `ent` - the entity the player right-clicked
* table `tr` - the player's eye trace

fields.name: OnCreate
fields.description:
Same as `MenuOpen`, but also called for toggle properties and has different arguments. This is called immediately after `MenuOpen`, but nothing happens in between so you should only ever use one or the other.


Function argument(s):
* table `self` - the property table
* DMenu `menu` - the property menu
* DMenuOption `option` - the menu option

entries.name: PropSelect
entries.description:
Used in Sandbox tools to allow the player to select models out of a list. Despite being only used in Sandbox, it is **not** exclusive to that gamemode.

See also [MatSelect](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/MatSelect) for the material selecting alternative.

entries.name: AddModel
entries.description: Adds a new model to the selection list.

args.name: model
args.description: Model path, **including** `models/` and `.mdl`.

args.name: convars
args.description: A list of convar names (as keys) and their values to set when the user selects this model.

entries.name: AddModelEx
entries.description: Adds a new model to the selection list.

args.name: value
args.description: The "value" for this model, which is used to set the ContextBase:SetConVar.

args.name: model
args.description: Model path, **including** `models/` and `.mdl`.

args.name: skin
args.description: The skin number for this model. It will **not** be set to the convar, use the value argument to track skin-model combos.

entries.name: FindAndSelectButton
entries.description: Find and select a [SpawnIcon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/SpawnIcon) panel based on the input model path.

args.name: mdl
args.description: The model to find and select within this PropSelect.

entries.name: FindModelByValue
entries.description: Find a [SpawnIcon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/SpawnIcon) panel based on the input model path.

args.name: mdl
args.description: The model to find within this PropSelect.

returns.description: The found spawnicon, or `nil`.

entries.name: RadioButton
entries.description:
**INTERNAL**: This is used internally - although you're able to use it you probably shouldn't.

		
		Currently there are no functions to retrieve checked state of a Radio Button, and their visuals are seemingly broken.

entries.name: ragdoll_dissolved
entries.description: Called when a Ragdoll is going to be Dissolved.

fields.name: entindex
fields.description: The Entity:EntIndex of the disolved Ragdoll.

entries.name: render
entries.description: The render library is a powerful set of functions that let you control how the world and its contents are rendered. It can also be used to draw some 3D clientside effects such as beams, boxes and spheres.

entries.name: AddBeam
entries.description:
Adds a Beam Segment to the Beam started by [render.StartBeam](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.StartBeam).

		For more detailed information on Beams, as well as usage examples, see the [Beams Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_beams).

args.name: startPos
args.description: Beam start position.

args.name: width
args.description: The width of the beam.

args.name: textureEnd
args.description: The end coordinate of the texture used.

args.name: color
args.description: The color to be used.

entries.name: BindLocalCubemap
entries.description:
Binds a given texture as a cubemap. The texture given must be a cubemap texture.

This is useful in context of drawing models manually ([Entity:DrawModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:DrawModel)), especially in GUI applications.

args.name: texName
args.description:
The path to the texture (`.vtf`) to use, e.g. `editor/cubemap`.

The function will automatically select the `.hdr` version of the texture based on player's current settings.

Set to `nil` to unbind a cubemap, which will result in pitch black cubemap.

entries.name: BlurRenderTarget
entries.description:
Blurs the render target ( or a given texture ).
		
		**WARNING**: Calling this on a RenderTarget created with TEXTUREFLAGS_POINTSAMPLE will result in strange visual glitching.

args.name: rendertarget
args.description: The texture to blur.

args.name: blurx
args.description: Horizontal amount of blur.

args.name: blury
args.description: Vertical amount of blur.

args.name: passes
args.description: Amount of passes to go through.

entries.name: BrushMaterialOverride
entries.description: This function overrides the brush material for next render operations. It can be used with [Entity:DrawModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:DrawModel).

entries.name: Capture
entries.description:
Captures a part of the current render target and returns the data as a binary string in the given format.

Since the pixel buffer clears itself every frame, this will return a black screen outside of render hooks. To capture the user's final view, use [GM:PostRender](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PostRender). This will not capture the Steam overlay or third-party injections (such as the Discord overlay, Overwolf, and advanced cheats) on the user's screen.

**WARNING**: In PNG mode, this function can produce unexpected result where foreground is rendered as transparent.
This is caused by [render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha) set to `true` when doing most of render operations, including rendering in `_rt_fullframefb`. If you want to capture render target's content as PNG image only for output quality, set [Structures/RenderCaptureData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/RenderCaptureData)'s `alpha` to `false` when capturing render targets with [render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha) set to `true`.


**WARNING**: This function will return nil if escape menu is open.

args.name: captureData
args.description: Parameters of the capture. See Structures/RenderCaptureData.

returns.description: The binary data.

entries.name: CapturePixels
entries.description:
Dumps the current render target and allows the pixels to be accessed by [render.ReadPixel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ReadPixel). 

	Capturing outside a render hook will return an image filled with `0 0 0 255`.

	See also [render.Capture](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.Capture).

entries.name: Clear
entries.description:
Clears the current render target and the specified buffers.

This sets the alpha incorrectly for [surface](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/surface) draw calls for render targets.

args.name: r
args.description: Red component to clear to.

args.name: g
args.description: Green component to clear to.

args.name: b
args.description: Blue component to clear to.

args.name: a
args.description: Alpha component to clear to.

args.name: clearDepth
args.description: Clear the depth.

args.name: clearStencil
args.description: Clear the stencil.

entries.name: ClearBuffersObeyStencil
entries.description:
Tests every pixel of the active [Render Target](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_rendertargets) against the current Stencil configuration and sets the Color Channel values and, optionally, the Depth Buffer values for every pixel that passes.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page

		**NOTE**: This function does **not** clear the Stencil Buffer on its own.  
			If you would like to clear the Stencil Buffer, you can use [render.ClearStencil](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ClearStencil).

args.name: red
args.description:
The red Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

args.name: green
args.description:
The green Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

args.name: blue
args.description:
The blue Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

args.name: alpha
args.description:
The alpha (translucency) Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

args.name: clearDepth
args.description: If true, reset the Depth Buffer values.

entries.name: ClearDepth
entries.description: Resets the depth buffer.

args.name: clearStencil
args.description: Whether to also clear the stencil buffer.

entries.name: ClearRenderTarget
entries.description:
Clears a render target.

It uses [render.Clear](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.Clear) then [render.SetRenderTarget](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetRenderTarget) on the modified render target.

args.name: color
args.description: The color.

entries.name: ClearStencil
entries.description:
Sets the Stencil Buffer value to `0` for all pixels in the currently active [Render Target](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_rendertargets).
		
		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

entries.name: ClearStencilBufferRectangle
entries.description:
Sets the Stencil Buffer value for every pixel in a given rectangle to a given value.

This is **not** affected by [render.SetStencilWriteMask](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilWriteMask).

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: startX
args.description: The X coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle to be cleared.

args.name: startY
args.description: The Y coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle to be cleared.

args.name: endX
args.description:
The X coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle to be cleared.  
			**Note:** Unlike some other rectangle-based functions, this is **not** the width of the rectangle.

args.name: endY
args.description:
The Y coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle to be cleared.  
			**Note:** Unlike some other rectangle-based functions, this is **not** the height of the rectangle.

args.name: stencilBufferValue
args.description: The Stencil Buffer value that all pixels within the rectangle will be set to.

entries.name: ComputeDynamicLighting
entries.description:
Calculates the lighting caused by dynamic lights (such as [Global.DynamicLight](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.DynamicLight) and the Light Sandbox tool) for the specified surface. This will not include map ambient light.

See also [render.ComputeLighting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ComputeLighting) for a function that also includes map's ambient lighting.

args.name: position
args.description: The position to sample from.

args.name: normal
args.description: The normal of the surface.

returns.description: A vector representing the light at that point.

entries.name: ComputeLighting
entries.description:
Calculates the light color at a certain position.

This includes both ambient light and dynamic light.

See [render.ComputeDynamicLighting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ComputeDynamicLighting) for dynamic light only.

See [render.GetAmbientLightColor](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.GetAmbientLightColor) for map-wide ambient color.

args.name: position
args.description: The position to get the light at.

args.name: normal
args.description:
The direction of an imaginary surface to get the light at.

Pointing away from walls will get the lighting the wall receives. Pointing towards walls will not.

returns.description: A vector representing the light at that point.

entries.name: ComputePixelDiameterOfSphere
entries.description: Calculates diameter of a 3D sphere on a 2D screen.

args.name: point
args.description: The position of the sphere in 3D space.

args.name: radius
args.description: The radius of the sphere in 3D space.

returns.description: The diameter of the sphere in 2D screen space.

entries.name: CopyRenderTargetToTexture
entries.description:
Copies the currently active Render Target to the specified texture.
		**WARNING**: This does not copy the Depth buffer, no method for that is known at this moment so a common workaround is to store the source texture somewhere else, perform your drawing operations, save the result somewhere else and reapply the source texture.

args.name: Target
args.description: The texture to copy to.

entries.name: CopyTexture
entries.description:
Copies the contents of one texture to another. Only works with rendertargets.
		**WARNING**: This does not copy the Depth buffer, no method for that is known at this moment so a common workaround is to store the source texture somewhere else, perform your drawing operations, save the result somewhere else and reapply the source texture.

args.name: texture_from
args.description: The texture to copy from.

args.name: texture_to
args.description: The texture being copied to.

entries.name: CullMode
entries.description: Sets the cull mode. The culling mode defines how back faces are culled when rendering geometry.

args.name: cullMode
args.description: Cullmode, see Enums/MATERIAL_CULLMODE.

entries.name: DepthRange
entries.description:
Set's the depth range of the upcoming render.
**NOTE**: Viewmodels get drawn with a depth range of `0` to `0.1` instead of the normal `0` to `1`. Incorrectly resetting the value can cause rendering issues.

args.name: depthmin
args.description: The minimum depth of the upcoming render. `0.0` = render normally; `1.0` = render nothing.

args.name: depthmax
args.description: The maximum depth of the upcoming render. `0.0` = render everything (through walls); `1.0` = render normally.

entries.name: DrawBeam
entries.description:
Draws a single-segment Beam made out of a textured, billboarded quad stretching between two points.

		For more detailed information, including usage examples, see the [Beams Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_beams).

args.name: startPos
args.description: The Beam's start position.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The Beam's end position.

args.name: width
args.description: The width of the Beam.

args.name: textureStart
args.description: The starting coordinate of the Beam's texture.

args.name: textureEnd
args.description: The end coordinate of the Beam's texture.

args.name: color
args.description: What Color to tint the Beam.

entries.name: DrawBox
entries.description: Draws a box in 3D space.

args.name: position
args.description: Origin of the box.

args.name: angles
args.description: Orientation of the box.

args.name: mins
args.description: Start position of the box, relative to origin.

args.name: maxs
args.description: End position of the box, relative to origin.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the box.

entries.name: DrawLine
entries.description: Draws a line in 3D space.

args.name: startPos
args.description: Line start position in world coordinates.

args.name: endPos
args.description: Line end position in world coordinates.

args.name: color
args.description: The color to be used. Uses Color.

args.name: writeZ
args.description:
Whether or not to consider the Z buffer. If false, the line will be drawn over everything currently drawn, if true, the line will be drawn with depth considered, as if it were a regular object in 3D space.

Enabling this option will cause the line to ignore the color's alpha.

entries.name: DrawQuad
entries.description: Draws 2 connected triangles. Expects material to be set by [render.SetMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetMaterial).

args.name: vert1
args.description: First vertex.

args.name: vert2
args.description: The second vertex.

args.name: vert3
args.description: The third vertex.

args.name: vert4
args.description: The fourth vertex.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the quad.

entries.name: DrawQuadEasy
entries.description: Draws a quad. Expects material to be set by [render.SetMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetMaterial).

args.name: position
args.description: Origin of the sprite.

args.name: normal
args.description: The face direction of the quad.

args.name: width
args.description: The width of the quad.

args.name: height
args.description: The height of the quad.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the quad.

args.name: rotation
args.description: The rotation of the quad counter-clockwise in degrees around the normal axis. In other words, the quad will always face the same way but this will rotate its corners.

entries.name: DrawScreenQuad
entries.description:
Draws the current material set by [render.SetMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetMaterial) to the whole screen. The color cannot be customized.

See also [render.DrawScreenQuadEx](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawScreenQuadEx).

args.name: applyPoster
args.description: If set to true, when rendering a poster the quad will be properly drawn in parts in the poster. This is used internally by some Post Processing effects. Certain special textures (frame buffer like textures) do not need this adjustment.

entries.name: DrawScreenQuadEx
entries.description:
Draws the current material set by [render.SetMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetMaterial) to the area specified. Color cannot be customized.

See also [render.DrawScreenQuad](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawScreenQuad).

args.name: startX
args.description: X start position of the rect.

args.name: startY
args.description: Y start position of the rect.

args.name: width
args.description: Width of the rect.

args.name: height
args.description: Height of the rect.

entries.name: DrawSphere
entries.description:
Draws a sphere in 3D space. The material previously set with [render.SetMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetMaterial) will be applied the sphere's surface.

See also [render.DrawWireframeSphere](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawWireframeSphere) for a wireframe equivalent.

args.name: position
args.description: Position of the sphere.

args.name: radius
args.description: Radius of the sphere. Negative radius will make the sphere render inwards rather than outwards.

args.name: longitudeSteps
args.description: The number of longitude steps. This controls the quality of the sphere. Higher quality will lower performance significantly. 50 is a good number to start with.

args.name: latitudeSteps
args.description: The number of latitude steps. This controls the quality of the sphere. Higher quality will lower performance significantly. 50 is a good number to start with.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the sphere.

entries.name: DrawSprite
entries.description: Draws a sprite in 3D space.

args.name: position
args.description: Position of the sprite.

args.name: width
args.description: Width of the sprite.

args.name: height
args.description: Height of the sprite.

args.name: color
args.description: Color of the sprite.

entries.name: DrawTextureToScreen
entries.description: Draws a texture over the whole screen.

args.name: tex
args.description: The texture to draw.

entries.name: DrawTextureToScreenRect
entries.description: Draws a textured rectangle.

args.name: tex
args.description: The texture to draw.

args.name: x
args.description: The x coordinate of the rectangle to draw.

args.name: y
args.description: The y coordinate of the rectangle to draw.

args.name: width
args.description: The width of the rectangle to draw.

args.name: height
args.description: The height of the rectangle to draw.

entries.name: DrawWireframeBox
entries.description: Draws a wireframe box in 3D space.

args.name: position
args.description: Position of the box.

args.name: angle
args.description: Angles of the box.

args.name: mins
args.description: The lowest corner of the box.

args.name: maxs
args.description: The highest corner of the box.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the box.

args.name: writeZ
args.description: Sets whenever to write to the zBuffer.

entries.name: DrawWireframeSphere
entries.description: Draws a wireframe sphere in 3d space.

args.name: position
args.description: Position of the sphere.

args.name: radius
args.description: The size of the sphere.

args.name: longitudeSteps
args.description:
The amount of longitude steps. 
The larger this number is, the smoother the sphere is.

args.name: latitudeSteps
args.description:
The amount of latitude steps. 
The larger this number is, the smoother the sphere is.

args.name: color
args.description: The color of the wireframe.

args.name: writeZ
args.description: Whether or not to consider the Z buffer. If false, the wireframe will be drawn over everything currently drawn. If true, it will be drawn with depth considered, as if it were a regular object in 3D space.

entries.name: EnableClipping
entries.description:
Sets the status of the clip renderer, returning previous state.

**WARNING**: To prevent unintended rendering behavior of other mods/the game, you must reset the clipping state to its previous value.

args.name: state
args.description: New clipping state.

returns.description: Previous clipping state.

entries.name: EndBeam

entries.name: GetAmbientLightColor
entries.description:
Returns the ambient color intensity of the map, basically the color the sky emits.

This is used by the engine to calculate shadow color using the following formula: `ambientLight * 3 + Vector( 0.3, 0.3, 0.3 )`

See also [render.ComputeLighting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ComputeLighting).

This is computed at map compile time and is stored in "linear color space".

See [render.WorldMaterialOverride](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.WorldMaterialOverride), [render.BrushMaterialOverride](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.BrushMaterialOverride) and [render.ModelMaterialOverride](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ModelMaterialOverride) for similar functions.

**WARNING**: In certain scenarios such as during entity's shadow pass, using this function can cause unexpected side effects. See example below on how to deal with this.

[render.MaterialOverride](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.MaterialOverride) overrides effects of this function.

args.name: index
args.description: The index of the material to override, in range of 0 to 31. `nil` will reset all overrides.

entries.name: Model
entries.description:
Creates a new [Global.ClientsideModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel), renders it at the specified pos/ang, and removes it. Can also be given an existing [CSEnt](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/CSEnt) to reuse instead.

**NOTE**: This function is only meant to be used in a single render pass kind of scenario, if you need to render a model continuously, use a cached [Global.ClientsideModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) and provide it as a second argument.


Using this with a map model ([game.GetWorld](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/game.GetWorld)():[GetModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetModel)()) crashes the game.

args.name: settings
args.description:
Requires:
* string model - The model to draw.
* Vector pos - The position to draw the model at.
* Angle angle - The angles to draw the model at.

args.name: ent
args.description: If provided, this entity will be reused instead of creating a new one with Global.ClientsideModel. Note that the ent's model, position and angles will be changed, and Entity:SetNoDraw will be set to true.

entries.name: ModelMaterialOverride
entries.description:
Forces all future draw operations to use a specific [IMaterial](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/IMaterial).  
		
		Because this is independent of a specific [Entity](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity), it can be used to change materials on static models that are part of maps.

**WARNING**: In certain scenarios such as during entity's shadow pass, using this function can cause unexpected side effects. See example on [render.MaterialOverride](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.MaterialOverride) about dealing with this.

args.name: material
args.description: The IMaterial that will be used for all upcoming draw operations, or `nil` to stop overriding.

entries.name: OverrideAlphaWriteEnable
entries.description:
Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the alpha channel of the current render target.

See also [render.OverrideBlend](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.OverrideBlend).

**NOTE**: Doing [surface](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/surface) draw calls with alpha set to 0 is a no-op and will never have any effect.

args.name: enable
args.description: Enable or disable the override.

args.name: shouldWrite
args.description: If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the alpha channel or not. Has no effect if the previous argument is false.

entries.name: OverrideBlend
entries.description:
Overrides the way that the final color and alpha is calculated for each pixel affected by upcoming draw operations.

When a draw operation is performed, the rendering system examines each pixel that is affected by the draw operation and determines its new color by combining (or "Blending") the pixel's current color (Called the "Destination" or "Dst" color) with the new color produced by the draw operation (Called the "Source" or "Src" color.)

This function allows you to control the way that those two colors (The Source and Destination) are combined to produce the final pixel color.

It's important to know that while [Colors](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Color) use values in the range `(0-255)`, the color and alpha values used here are normalized to the range `(0-1)` so that they can be multiplied together to produce a value that is still in the range `(0-1)`.

args.name: enabled
args.description: Set to `true` to enable Blend Overrides.

args.name: sourceMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source color and alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: destinationMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination color and alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: blendingFunction
args.description:
After the Source and Destination color and alpha have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Blending Function which combines them into the final color and alpha for the pixel.  
			One of the Enums/BLENDFUNC enums.

args.name: enabled
args.description: Set to `true` to enable Blend Overrides.

args.name: sourceColorMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source color** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Color Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: destinationColorMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination color** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Color Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: colorBlendingFunction
args.description:
After the Source and Destination colors have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Color Blending Function which combines them into the final color and alpha for the pixel.  
			One of the Enums/BLENDFUNC enums.

args.name: sourceAlphaMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Alpha Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: destinationAlphaMultiplier
args.description:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Alpha Blending Function.  
			One of the Enums/BLEND enums.

args.name: alphaBlendingFunction
args.description: After the Source and Destination alphas have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Alpha Blending Function which combines them into the final alpha for the pixel.

args.name: enabled
args.description: Set to `false` to disable blend overrides.

entries.name: OverrideBlendFunc
entries.description:
Overrides the internal graphical functions used to determine the final color and alpha of a rendered texture.

See also [render.OverrideAlphaWriteEnable](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.OverrideAlphaWriteEnable).

**NOTE**: Doing [surface](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/surface) draw calls with alpha set to 0 is a no-op and will never have any effect.

args.name: enabled
args.description: true to enable, false to disable. No other arguments are required when disabling.

args.name: srcBlend
args.description: The source color blend function Enums/BLEND. Determines how a rendered texture's final color should be calculated.

args.name: srcBlendAlpha
args.description: The source alpha blend function Enums/BLEND. Determines how a rendered texture's final alpha should be calculated.

entries.deprecated: Use render.OverrideBlend instead.

entries.name: OverrideColorWriteEnable
entries.description: Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the color channel of the current render target.

args.name: enable
args.description: Enable or disable the override.

args.name: shouldWrite
args.description: If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the color channel or not. Anything drawn after will still write to depth if enabled and shouldWrite is false.

entries.name: OverrideDepthEnable
entries.description: Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the depth buffer.

entries.name: PerformFullScreenStencilOperation
entries.description:
Performs a Stencil operation on every pixel in the active [Render Target](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_rendertargets) without performing a draw operation.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

entries.name: PopCustomClipPlane
entries.description: Removes the current active clipping plane from the clip plane stack.

entries.name: PopFilterMag
entries.description:
Pops (Removes) the texture filter most recently pushed (Added) onto the magnification texture filter stack.  
		
		This function should only be called *after* a magnification filter has been pushed via [render.PushFilterMag](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PushFilterMag).

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

entries.name: PopFilterMin
entries.description:
Pops (Removes) the texture filter most recently pushed (Added) onto the minification texture filter stack.  
		
		This function should only be called *after* a minification filter has been pushed via [render.PushFilterMin()](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PushFilterMin).

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

entries.name: PopFlashlightMode
entries.description: Pops the current flashlight mode from the flashlight mode stack.

entries.name: PopRenderTarget
entries.description:
Pops the last render target and viewport from the RT stack and sets them as the current render target and viewport.

This is should be called to restore the previous render target and viewport after a call to [render.PushRenderTarget](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PushRenderTarget).

entries.name: PushCustomClipPlane
entries.description:
Pushes a new clipping plane of the clip plane stack and sets it as active.

A max of 2 clip planes are supported on Linux/POSIX, and 6 on Windows.

args.name: normal
args.description: The normal of the clipping plane.

args.name: distance
args.description: The distance of the plane from the world origin. You can use Vector:Dot between the normal and any point on the plane to find this.

entries.name: PushFilterMag
entries.description:
Pushes (Adds) a texture filter onto the magnification texture filter stack.  
		This will modify how textures are stretched to sizes larger than their native resolution for upcoming rendering and drawing operations.  
		For a version of this same function that modifies filtering for texture sizes smaller than their native resolution, see [render.PushFilterMin](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PushFilterMin)

		Always be sure to call [render.PopFilterMag](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PopFilterMag) afterwards to avoid texture filtering problems.

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

If current texture has more than 1 mipmap, this also sets the mipmap filter.

args.name: texFilterType
args.description: The texture filter to use. For available options, see Enums/TEXFILTER.

entries.name: PushFilterMin
entries.description:
Pushes (Adds) a texture filter onto the minification texture filter stack.  
		This will modify how textures are compressed to a lower resolution than their native resolution for upcoming rendering and drawing operations.  
		For a version of this same function that modifies filtering for texture sizes larger than their native resolution, see [render.PushFilterMag()](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PushFilterMag)

		Always be sure to call [render.PopFilterMin()](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PopFilterMin) afterwards to avoid texture filtering problems.

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

args.name: texFilterType
args.description: The texture filter to use. For available options, see Enums/TEXFILTER.

entries.name: PushFlashlightMode
entries.description: Enables the flashlight projection for the upcoming rendering.

args.name: enable
args.description: Whether the flashlight mode should be enabled or disabled.

entries.deprecated: This will leave models lit under specific conditions. You should use render.RenderFlashlights which is meant as a direct replacement for this function.

entries.name: PushRenderTarget
entries.description:
Pushes the current render target and viewport to the RT stack then sets a new current render target and viewport. If the viewport is not specified, the dimensions of the render target are used instead.

This is similar to a call to [render.SetRenderTarget](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetRenderTarget) and [render.SetViewPort](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetViewPort) where the current render target and viewport have been saved beforehand, except the viewport isn't clipped to screen bounds.

See also [render.PopRenderTarget](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.PopRenderTarget).

**NOTE**: If you want to render to the render target in 2d mode and it is not the same size as the screen, use [cam.Start2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start2D) and [cam.End2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.End2D).

**NOTE**: If the render target is bigger than the screen, rendering done with the surface library will be clipped to the screen bounds unless you call [Global.DisableClipping](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.DisableClipping)

args.name: texture
args.description:
The new render target to be used.  
			Can be set to `nil` to push the main game frame buffer.

args.description: X origin of the viewport.

args.name: y
args.description: Y origin of the viewport.

args.name: w
args.description: Width of the viewport.

args.name: h
args.description: Height of the viewport.

entries.name: RenderView
entries.description:
Renders the scene with the specified viewData to the current active render target.

Static props and LODs are rendered improperly due to incorrectly perceived distance.
Using render.RenderView on a RenderTarget texture in a 3d context like SWEP:PostDrawViewModel() while drawing the RenderTarget texture causes screen flickers.

entries.name: SetBlend
entries.description:
Sets the alpha blending (or transparency) for upcoming render operations.
	
See [render.SetColorModulation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetColorModulation) for the function to affect RGB color channels.

By itself, this will cause visible overlapping on parts of a model that are in front of other parts of the same model.  
For a solution to this, see the examples below.

This does not affect non-model `render.Draw*` functions.
**NOTE**: If a material has the [$alphatest](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/$alphatest) flag enabled then this function might not behave as expected because alpha will be binary, this has a default cutoff of `0.7`.

args.name: blending
args.description:
The alpha (transparency) for upcoming draw operations.  
			A value in the range `(0-1)` where `0` is fully transparent, `0.5` is 50% visible, and `1` is fully opaque.

entries.name: SetColorMaterial
entries.description:
Sets the current drawing material to "color".

The material is defined as:
```

 "UnlitGeneric"
 {
 	"$basetexture" "color/white"
 	"$model" 		1
 	"$translucent" 	1
 	"$vertexalpha" 	1
 	"$vertexcolor" 	1
 }
```

entries.name: SetColorMaterialIgnoreZ
entries.description:
Sets the current drawing material to `color_ignorez`.

The material is defined as:
```

 "UnlitGeneric"
 {
 	"$basetexture" "color/white"
  	"$model" 		1
 	"$translucent" 	1
 	"$vertexalpha" 	1
 	"$vertexcolor" 	1
 	"$ignorez"		1
 }
```

entries.name: SetLocalModelLights
entries.description:
Sets up the local lighting for any upcoming render operation. Up to 4 local lights can be defined, with one of three different types (point, directional, spot).

Disables all local lights if called with no arguments.

See also [render.SetModelLighting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetModelLighting) for "lightbox" lighting. They are not mutually exclusive.

entries.name: SetModelLighting
entries.description:
Sets up the ambient lighting for any upcoming render operation. Ambient lighting can be seen as a cube enclosing the object to be drawn, each of its faces representing a directional light source that shines towards the object. Thus, there is a total of six different light sources that can be configured separately.

Light color components are not restricted to a specific range (i.e. 0-1), instead, higher values will result in a brighter light.

[render.ResetModelLighting](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.ResetModelLighting) will set all 6 directions at once.
See also [render.SetLocalModelLights](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetLocalModelLights).

args.name: lightDirection
args.description: The light source to edit, see Enums/BOX.

args.name: red
args.description: The red component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

args.name: green
args.description: The green component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

args.name: blue
args.description: The blue component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

entries.name: SetRenderTargetEx
entries.description:
Sets the render target with the specified index of `COLOR[n]` to the specified rt, allowing you to work with [Multiple Render Targets (MRT)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d9/multiple-render-targets). Since standard shaders don't use MRT, you might find this useful at [Shaders/screenspace_general](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Shaders/screenspace_general).
**NOTE**: MRT doesn't work with 2D render functions like [render.DrawScreenQuad](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawScreenQuad). Instead, you can render a [render.DrawQuad](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawQuad) using [cam.Start2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start2D).

**WARNING**: If you try to render with MSAA and set the main RenderTarget with another RenderTarget, nothing will be rendered.

[Link to Direct3D 9 documentation on MRT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d9/multiple-render-targets#:~:text=No%20antialiasing%20is%20supported)

`Multiple render targets have the following restrictions:`
* *No antialiasing is supported.*

args.name: rtIndex
args.description: The index of output `COLOR[n]` [semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-semantics) from pixel-shader. Min: `0`, max: `3`.

entries.name: SetStencilCompareFunction
entries.description:
Sets the Compare Function that all pixels affected by a draw operation will have their Stencil Buffer value tested against.  

When not set to a static value like NEVER or ALWAYS, the Stencil Buffer value corresponding to each affected pixel will be compared against the current [Reference Value](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilReferenceValue).

Pixels that **Pass** the Compare Function check move on to the Depth Test, which determines if the draw operation will ultimately be allowed to overwrite the pixel's Color Channel, Stencil Buffer, and Depth Buffer values.

Pixels that **Fail** the Compare Function check have the [Fail Operation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation) performed on their Stencil Buffer value and do **not** have any of their Render Target layers modified by the draw operation.

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: compareFunction
args.description: The Compare Function that each affected pixel's Stencil Buffer value will be evaluated against during a draw operation.

entries.name: SetStencilEnable
entries.description:
Enables or disables the Stencil system for future draw operations.

While enabled, all pixels affected by draw operations will have their corresponding values in the active [Render Target's](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_rendertargets) Stencil Buffer compared against the current [Reference Value](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilReferenceValue) and their current Depth Buffer value compared against the depth of the corresponding pixel from the draw operation.  
Depending on the outcomes of these comparisons, one of either the [Pass](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation), [Fail](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation), or [Z-Fail](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilZFailOperation) operations is performed on the pixel's Stencil Buffer value.  
A pixel will only be updated in the active [Render Target](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_rendertargets) if the [Pass Operation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation) is performed.

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

**NOTE**: The Stencil system's configuration does **not** reset automatically.  
To prevent unexpected behavior, always manually ensure that the Stencil system is configured appropriately for your use-case after enabling it.

args.name: newState
args.description: The new state.

entries.name: SetStencilFailOperation
entries.description:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) did **not** [Pass](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation) the pixel.  

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: failOperation
args.description: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function does not Pass a pixel.

entries.name: SetStencilPassOperation
entries.description:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) Passes the pixel.  

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: passOperation
args.description: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function Passes a pixel.

entries.name: SetStencilReferenceValue
entries.description:
Sets the Stencil system's Reference Value which is compared against each pixel's corresponding Stencil Buffer value in the [Compare Function](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) and can be used to modify the Stencil Buffer value of those same pixels in the [Pass](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation), [Fail](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation), and [Z Fail](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilZFailOperation) operations.
		
		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: referenceValue
args.description:
The value that the Compare function and the pass, fail, and z-fail operations will use.  
			This is an 8-bit (`byte`) unsigned integer value in the range [`0-255`].

entries.name: SetStencilTestMask
entries.description:
Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are read (tested) from the Stencil Buffer

		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.

		This is a companion function to [render.SetStencilWriteMask](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilWriteMask) which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are written.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: bitMask
args.description:
The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
			Set to `255` to make no change to read Stencil Buffer values.

entries.name: SetStencilWriteMask
entries.description:
Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are written to the Stencil Buffer

		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.

		This is a companion function to [render.SetStencilTestMask](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilTestMask) which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are read.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: bitMask
args.description:
The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
			Set to `255` to make no change to written Stencil Buffer values.

entries.name: SetStencilZFailOperation
entries.description:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) Passed a given pixel, but it did **not** Pass the Depth Test.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render_stencils) page.

args.name: zFailOperation
args.description: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function Passes a pixel, but the pixel fails the Depth Test.
