Entity class name of the SWEP (file or folder name of your SWEP). This is
            set automatically

fields.name: ClassNameOverride
fields.description: If set, overrides the classname of the SWEP.

fields.name: Category
fields.description:
The spawn menu category that this weapon
            resides in.

fields.name: SubCategory
fields.description: Optional spawnmenu sub-category to put this weapon into.

fields.name: Spawnable
fields.description:
Whether or not this weapon can be obtained through the
            spawn menu.

fields.name: AdminOnly
fields.description:
If spawnable, this variable determines whether only
            administrators can use the button in the spawn menu.

fields.name: PrintName
fields.description: The name of the SWEP displayed in the spawn menu.

fields.name: Base
fields.description: The weapon's base script, relative to `lua/weapons`.

fields.name: m_WeaponDeploySpeed
fields.description:
The deploy speed multiplier. This does not change the
            internal deployment speed.

fields.name: Owner
fields.description: Use [Entity:GetOwner](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetOwner)() instead.

fields.name: Weapon
fields.deprecated: Use `SWEP` instead. However, if called in a SWEP method; use `self` instead.
fields.description: Use `SWEP` instead. However, if called in a SWEP method; use `self` instead.

fields.name: Author
fields.description: The SWEP's author.

fields.name: Contact
fields.description: The contact information regarding the SWEP's author.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.description: The purpose of the SWEP.

fields.name: Instructions
fields.description: The instructions regarding the SWEP's usage.

fields.name: ViewModel
fields.description: Relative path to the SWEP's view model.

fields.name: ViewModelFlip
fields.description: Used primarily for Counter Strike: Source view models, this variable is used to flip them back to normal.

fields.name: ViewModelFlip1
fields.description: Behaves similarly to `ViewModelFlip`, but for the second view model.

fields.name: ViewModelFlip2
fields.description: Behaves similarly to `ViewModelFlip`, but for the third view model.

fields.name: ViewModelFOV
fields.description: The field of view percieved whilst wielding this `SWEP`.

fields.name: WorldModel
fields.description: Relative path to the SWEP's world model.

fields.name: AutoSwitchFrom
fields.description:
Whether this weapon can be autoswitched
            away from when the player runs out of ammo in this weapon or picks up another weapon or ammo

fields.name: AutoSwitchTo
fields.description:
Whether this weapon can be autoswitched to
            when the player runs out of ammo in their current weapon or they pick this weapon up

fields.name: Weight
fields.description:
Determines the priority of the weapon when
            autoswitching. The weapon being autoswitched from will attempt to switch to a weapon with the same weight
            that has ammo, but if none exists, it will prioritise higher weight weapons.

fields.name: BobScale
fields.description:
The scale of the viewmodel bob (viewmodel movement
            from left to right when walking around)

fields.name: SwayScale
fields.description:
The scale of the viewmodel sway (viewmodel
            position lerp when looking around).

fields.name: BounceWeaponIcon
fields.description:
Should the weapon icon bounce in weapon
            selection?

fields.name: DrawWeaponInfoBox
fields.description:
Should draw the weapon selection info
            box, containing SWEP.Instructions, etc.

fields.name: DrawAmmo
fields.description: Should we draw the default HL2 ammo counter?

fields.name: DrawCrosshair
fields.description: Should we draw the default crosshair?

fields.name: RenderGroup
fields.description: The SWEP render group, see Enums/RENDERGROUP. If unset, the engine will decide the render group based on the SWEPs world model.

fields.name: WantsTranslucency
fields.description:
If set and `RenderGroup` is not, will switch the render group to Enums/RENDERGROUP#RENDERGROUP_BOTH when appropriate.

See Structures/ENT for details.

fields.name: Slot
fields.description: Slot in the weapon selection menu, starts with `0`

fields.name: SlotPos
fields.description: Position in the slot, should be in the range `0-128`

fields.name: SpeechBubbleLid
fields.description: Internal variable for drawing the info box in weapon selection

fields.name: WepSelectIcon
fields.description:
Path to
            a material. Override this in your SWEP to set the icon in the weapon selection. This must be the texture ID,
            see surface.GetTextureID. Keep in mind that the path must be to a `.vmt` file, NOT `.vtf`.


Alternatively you can render custom weapon selection via WEAPON:DrawWeaponSelection.

fields.name: CSMuzzleFlashes
fields.description:
Should we use Counter-Strike muzzle
            flashes upon firing? This is required for DoD:S or CS:S view models to fix their muzzle flashes.

fields.name: CSMuzzleX
fields.description:
Use the X shape muzzle flash instead of the
            default Counter-Strike muzzle flash. Requires Structures/SWEP#CSMuzzleFlashes to be set to true.

fields.name: Primary
fields.description:
Primary attack settings. The table contains these fields:

* string `Ammo` - Ammo type (`Pistol`, `SMG1`, etc.) See game.AddAmmoType.
* number `ClipSize` - The maximum amount of bullets one clip can hold. Setting it to `-1` means weapon uses no clips, like a grenade or a rocket launch.
* number `DefaultClip` - Default ammo in the clip, making it higher than ClipSize will give player additional ammo on spawn
* boolean `Automatic` - If true makes the weapon shoot automatically as long as the player has primary attack button held down

fields.name: Secondary
fields.description: Secondary attack settings, has same fields as Primary attack settings

fields.name: UseHands
fields.description:
Makes the player models hands bonemerged onto
            the view model

            The gamemode and view models **must** support this feature for it to work!
                You can find more information here: [Using Viewmodel Hands](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Using_Viewmodel_Hands)

fields.name: Folder
fields.description:
The folder from where the weapon was loaded. This should always be
            "weapons/weapon_myweapon", regardless whether your SWEP is stored as a file, or multiple files in a folder.
            It is set automatically on load

fields.name: AccurateCrosshair
fields.description:
Makes the default SWEP crosshair be
            positioned in 3D space where your aim actually is (like on Jeep), instead of simply sitting in the middle of
            the screen at all times

fields.name: DisableDuplicator
fields.description:
Disable the ability for players to duplicate this
            SWEP

fields.name: ScriptedEntityType
fields.description:
Sets the spawnmenu content icon type
            for the entity, used by spawnmenu in the Sandbox-derived gamemodes.
            See spawnmenu.AddContentType for more information.

fields.name: m_bPlayPickupSound
fields.description:
If set to false, the weapon will not play the
            weapon pick up sound when picked up.

fields.name: IconOverride
fields.description:
If set,
            overrides the icon path to be displayed in the Spawnmenu for this entity. The path is relative to the `materials/` folder.

entries.name: system
entries.description: The system library provides functions that allow you to gather information about the system running the game, such as operating system, uptime and battery level.

entries.name: AppTime
entries.description:
Returns the total uptime of the current application as reported by Steam.

This will return a similar value to [Global.SysTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.SysTime).

**NOTE**: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

returns.description: Seconds of game uptime as an integer.

entries.name: BatteryPower
entries.description: Returns the current battery power.

returns.description:
0-100 if a battery (laptop, UPS, etc) is present.

Will instead return 255 if plugged in without a battery.

entries.name: FlashWindow
entries.description: Flashes the window, turning the border to white briefly

entries.name: GetCountry
entries.description:
Returns the country code of this computer, determined by the IP of the client. Uses the steamworks API function `SteamUtils()->GetIPCountry()`.

**NOTE**: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

returns.description: Two-letter country code, using [ISO 3166-1](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) standard.

entries.name: HasFocus
entries.description:
Returns whether or not the game window has focus.

**NOTE**: This function does not work on dedicated servers and will instead return no value.

returns.description: Whether or not the game window has focus.

entries.name: IsLinux
entries.description: Returns whether the current OS is Linux.

returns.description: Whether or not the game is running on Linux.

entries.name: IsOSX
entries.description: Returns whether the current OS is OSX.

returns.description: Whether or not the game is running on OSX.

entries.name: IsWindowed
entries.description: Returns whether the game is being run in a window or in fullscreen (you can change this by opening the menu, clicking 'Options', then clicking the 'Video' tab, and changing the Display Mode using the dropdown menu):

returns.description: Is the game running in a window?

entries.name: IsWindows
entries.description: Returns whether the current OS is Windows.

returns.description: Whether the system the game runs on is Windows or not.

entries.name: SteamTime
entries.description:
Returns the synchronized Steam time. This is the number of seconds since the [Unix epoch](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).

**NOTE**: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

returns.description: Current Steam-synchronized Unix time.

entries.name: UpTime
entries.description:
Returns the amount of seconds since the Steam user last moved their mouse.

This is a direct binding to ISteamUtils->GetSecondsSinceComputerActive, and is most likely related to Steam's automatic "Away" online status.

**NOTE**: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

returns.description: The amount of seconds since the Steam user last moved their mouse.

entries.name: table
entries.description:
The [table](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Beginner_Tutorial_Tables) **type** is an object that can store multiple values.

The table **library** is a standard Lua library which provides functions to manipulate tables. In Garry's Mod there are several extra useful functions added to this library.

This category lists the functions available in the table `library`.

entries.name: Add
entries.description:
Adds all values from `source` table into the `target` table. This is most useful for sequential tables, not "dictionary" or "map" tables. See [table.Merge](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Merge) if you want to merge 2 tables into one.

See [table.insert](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.insert) for a function that adds a single value, and [table.Inherit](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Inherit) for a function that inherits keys from one table to another.

args.name: target
args.description: The table to insert the new values into.

args.name: source
args.description: The table to retrieve the values from.

returns.description: The target table.

entries.name: ClearKeys
entries.description: Changes all keys to sequential integers. This creates a new table object and does not affect the original.

args.name: table
args.description: The original table to modify.

args.name: saveKeys
args.description: Save the keys within each member table. This will insert a new field `__key` into each value, and should not be used if the table contains non-table values.

returns.description: Table with integer keys.

entries.name: CollapseKeyValue
entries.description: Collapses a table with keyvalue structure

args.name: input
args.description: Input table

returns.description: Output table

entries.name: concat
entries.description: Concatenates the contents of a table to a string.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to concatenate.

args.name: concatenator
args.description: A separator to insert between strings

args.name: startPos
args.description: The key to start at

args.name: endPos
args.description: The key to end at

returns.description: Concatenated values

entries.name: Copy
entries.description:
Creates a deep copy and returns that copy.

**WARNING**: This function is very slow! If you know the table structure, it is better to write your own copying mechanism

**WARNING**: This function does NOT copy userdata, such as [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector)s and [Angle](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Angle)s!

args.name: originalTable
args.description: The table to be copied.

returns.description: A deep copy of the original table

entries.name: CopyFromTo
entries.description: Empties the target table, and merges all values from the source table into it.

args.name: source
args.description: The table to copy from.

args.name: target
args.description: The table to write to.

entries.name: Count
entries.description:
Counts the amount of keys in a table. This should only be used when a table is not numerically and sequentially indexed. For those tables, consider the length (**#**) operator.

If you only want to test if the table is empty or not, use [table.IsEmpty](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.IsEmpty) instead as it is a lot faster.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to count the keys of.

returns.description: The number of keyvalue pairs. This includes non-numeric and non-sequential keys, unlike the length (**#**) operator.

entries.name: DeSanitise
entries.description: Converts a table that has been sanitised with [table.Sanitise](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Sanitise) back to its original form

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to be de-sanitised

returns.description: De-sanitised table

entries.name: Empty
entries.description: Removes all values from a table. If your table is not a metatable, it is almost always better to use `tab = {}` to preserve performance.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to empty.

entries.name: FindNext
entries.description: Returns the value positioned after the supplied value in a table. If it isn't found then the first element in the table is returned

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to search

args.name: value
args.description: Value to return element after

returns.description: Found element

entries.deprecated: Instead, iterate the table using ipairs or increment from the previous index using Global.next. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered.

entries.name: FindPrev
entries.description: Returns the value positioned before the supplied value in a table. If it isn't found then the last element in the table is returned

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to search

args.name: value
args.description: Value to return element before

returns.description: Found element

entries.deprecated: Instead, iterate your table with ipairs, storing the previous value and checking for the target. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered.

entries.name: Flip
entries.description:
Flips key-value pairs of each element within a table, so that each value becomes the key, and each key becomes the value.

**WARNING**: Take care when using this function, as a Lua table cannot contain multiple instances of the same key. As such, data loss is possible when using this function on tables with duplicate values.

```
local test = { test = 1, test2 = 1 }
local f = table.Flip( test )
PrintTable( f )
-- Outputs "1	=	test2"
```

args.name: input
args.description: The table to flip items of.

returns.description: The flipped table.

entries.name: ForceInsert
entries.description: Inserts a value in to the given table even if the table is non-existent

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to insert value in to

args.name: value
args.description: Value to insert

returns.description: The supplied or created table

entries.name: ForEach
entries.description:
Iterates for each key-value pair in the table, calling the function with the key and value of the pair. If the function returns anything, the loop is broken.

The GLua interpretation of this is [table.ForEach](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.ForEach).

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to iterate over.

args.name: callback
args.description:
The function to run for each key and value.



Function argument(s):
* any `key` - The key of a key-value pair for this iteration.
* any `val` - The value of a key-value pair for this iteration.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: The key of a key-value pair for this iteration.

arguments.name: val
arguments.description: The value of a key-value pair for this iteration.

entries.deprecated: This was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and removed in 5.2. You should use Global.pairs instead.

entries.name: foreachi
entries.description:
Iterates for each numeric index in the table in order.

This is inherited from the original Lua implementation and is deprecated in Lua as of 5.1; see [here](http://lua-users.org/wiki/TableLibraryTutorial). You should use [Global.ipairs](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.ipairs)() instead.

args.name: table
args.description: The table to iterate over.

args.name: func
args.description: The function to run for each index.

entries.deprecated: This was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and removed in 5.2. You should use Global.ipairs() instead.

entries.name: GetFirstKey
entries.description: Returns the first key found in the given table

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to retrieve key from

returns.description: Key

entries.deprecated:
Instead, expect the first key to be 1.

Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a first key.

entries.name: GetFirstValue
entries.description: Returns the first value found in the given table

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to retrieve value from

returns.description: Value

entries.deprecated:
Instead, index the table with a key of 1.

Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a first key.

entries.name: GetKeys
entries.description: Returns all keys of a table.

args.name: tabl
args.description: The table to get keys of

returns.description: Table of keys

entries.name: GetLastKey
entries.description: Returns the last key found in the given table

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to retrieve key from

returns.description: Key

entries.deprecated: Instead, use the result of the length (#) operator, ensuring it is not zero. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a last key.

entries.name: GetLastValue
entries.description: Returns the last value found in the given table

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to retrieve value from

returns.description: Value

entries.deprecated: Instead, index the table with the result of the length (#) operator, ensuring it is not zero. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a last key.

entries.name: getn
entries.description: Returns the length of the table.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to check.

returns.description: Sequential length.

entries.deprecated: This function was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and is removed in 5.2. Use the length (#) operator instead.

entries.name: GetWinningKey
entries.description: Returns a key of the supplied table with the highest number value.

args.name: inputTable
args.description: The table to search in.

returns.description: winningKey

entries.name: HasValue
entries.description:
Checks if a table has a value.
**WARNING**: This function is **very inefficient for large tables** (O(n)) and should probably not be called in things that run each frame. Instead, consider a table structure such as example 2 below. Also see: [Tables: Bad Habits](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tables:_Bad_Habits)

**NOTE**: For optimization, functions that look for a value by sorting the table should never be needed if you work on a table that you built yourself.

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to check

args.name: value
args.description: Value to search for

returns.description: Returns true if the table has that value, false otherwise

entries.name: Inherit
entries.description:
Copies any missing data from `base` to `target`, and sets the `target`'s `BaseClass` member to the `base` table's pointer.

See [table.Merge](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Merge), which overrides existing values and doesn't add a BaseClass member.


See also [table.Add](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Add), which simply adds values of one table to another.

Sub-tables aren't inherited. The target's table value will take priority.

args.name: target
args.description: Table to copy data to

args.name: base
args.description: Table to copy data from

returns.description: Target

entries.name: insert
entries.description:
Inserts a value into a table at the end of the table or at the given position.
	**NOTE**: This function does not call the `__newindex` [metamethod](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Metamethods).

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to insert the variable into.

args.name: position
args.description: The position in the table to insert the variable. If the third argument is nil this argument becomes the value to insert at the end of given table.

args.name: value
args.description: The variable to insert into the table.

returns.description: The index the object was placed at.

entries.name: IsEmpty
entries.description:
Returns whether or not the given table is empty.

This works on both sequential and non-sequential tables, and is a lot faster for non-sequential tables than `table.Count(tbl) == 0`.

For sequential tables it is better to use `tab[1] == nil`.

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to check.

returns.description: Is empty?

entries.name: IsSequential
entries.description: Returns whether or not the table's keys are sequential

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to check

returns.description: Is sequential

entries.name: KeyFromValue
entries.description: Returns the first key found to be containing the supplied value

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to search

args.name: value
args.description: Value to search for

returns.description: Key

entries.name: KeysFromValue
entries.description: Returns a table of keys containing the supplied value

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to search

args.name: value
args.description: Value to search for

returns.description: Keys

entries.name: LowerKeyNames
entries.description: Returns a copy of the input table with all string keys converted to be lowercase recursively

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to convert

returns.description: New table

entries.name: maxn
entries.description: Returns the highest numerical key.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to search.

returns.description: The highest numerical key.

entries.name: MemberValuesFromKey
entries.description:
Returns an array of values of given with given key from each table of given table.

See also [table.KeysFromValue](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.KeysFromValue).

args.name: inputTable
args.description: The table to search in.

args.name: keyName
args.description: The key to lookup.

returns.description: A list of found values, or an empty table.

entries.name: Merge
entries.description:
**NOTE**: This function can cause a stack overflow under certain circumstances.

Recursively merges the key-value pairs of the `source` table with the key-value pairs in the `destination` table.

See [table.Inherit](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Inherit), which doesn't override existing values.


See also [table.Add](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.Add), which simply adds values of one table to another.

args.name: destination
args.description: The table you want the source table to merge with.

args.name: source
args.description: The table you want to merge with the destination table.

args.name: forceOverride
args.description: If `true`, does not recursively merge sub-tables, and simply replaces them.

returns.description: Destination table

entries.name: move
entries.description: Moves elements from one part of a table to another part a given table. This is similar to assigning elements from the source table to the destination table in multiple assignments.

args.name: sourceTbl
args.description: The source table from which the elements are to be moved.

args.name: from
args.description: The start index of the source range from which the elements are to be moved.

args.name: to
args.description: The end index of the source range until which the elements are to be moved.

args.name: dest
args.description: The index within the destination table where the moved elements should be inserted.

args.name: destTbl
args.description: The destination table to which the elements are to be moved. By default, this is the same as the source table.

returns.description: The modified destination table.

entries.name: Pack
entries.description: Packs a set of items into a table and returns the new table. It is meant as an alternative implementation of `table.pack` from newer versions of Lua.

args.name: items
args.description: The items to pack into a table.

returns.description: A table containing the `items`.
The amount of items that were added to the table.

entries.name: Random
entries.description:
Returns a random value from the supplied table.

**WARNING**: This function iterates over the given table **twice**, therefore with sequential tables you should instead use following:

```
mytable[ math.random( #mytable ) ]
```

args.name: haystack
args.description: The table to choose from.

returns.description: A random value from the table.
The key associated with the random value.

entries.name: remove
entries.description:
Removes a value from a table and shifts any other values down to fill the gap.
**NOTE**: Does nothing if index is less than 1 or greater than `#tbl`

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to remove the value from.

args.name: index
args.description: The index of the value to remove.

returns.description: The value that was removed.

entries.name: RemoveByValue
entries.description:
Removes the first instance of a given value from the specified table with [table.remove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.remove), then returns the key that the value was found at.

**WARNING**: Avoid usage of this function. It does not remove all instances of given value in the table, only the first found, and it does not work with non sequential tables!

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table that will be searched.

args.name: val
args.description: The value to find within the table.

returns.description: The key at which the value was found, or false if the value was not found.

entries.name: Reverse
entries.description: Returns a reversed copy of a sequential table. Any non-sequential and non-numeric keyvalue pairs will not be copied.

args.name: tbl
args.description: Table to reverse.

returns.description: A reversed copy of the table.

entries.name: Sanitise
entries.description:
Converts [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector)s, [Angle](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Angle)s and [boolean](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/boolean)s to be able to be converted to and from key-values via [util.TableToKeyValues](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TableToKeyValues).

[table.DeSanitise](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.DeSanitise) performs the opposite transformation.

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to sanitise

returns.description: Sanitised table

entries.name: Shuffle
entries.description: Performs an inline [Fisher-Yates shuffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Yates_shuffle) on the table in `O(n)` time

args.name: target
args.description: The table to shuffle.

entries.name: sort
entries.description:
Sorts a sequential table either ascending or by the given sort function.
**NOTE**: This function modifies the table you give to it and internally uses the [quick sort algorithm](http://www.lua.org/source/5.2/ltablib.c.html#sort).

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to sort.

args.name: sorter
args.description:
If specified, the sorting function.



Function argument(s):
* any `a` - Item A to test.
* any `b` - Item B to test.

Function return value(s):
* boolean `result` - Result of the comparison. Return true in this function if you want the first parameter to come first in the sorted array.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Result of the comparison. Return true in this function if you want the first parameter to come first in the sorted array.

entries.name: SortByKey
entries.description:
Returns a list of keys sorted based on values of those keys.

For normal sorting see [table.sort](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.sort).

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to sort. All values of this table must be of same type.

args.name: descending
args.description: Should the order be descending?

returns.description: A table of keys sorted by values from supplied table.

entries.name: SortByMember
entries.description: Sorts a table by a named member.

args.name: tab
args.description: Table to sort.

args.name: memberKey
args.description: The key used to identify the member.

args.name: ascending
args.description: Whether or not the order should be ascending.

entries.name: SortDesc
entries.description:
Sorts a table in reverse order from [table.sort](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table.sort).
**NOTE**: This function modifies the table you give to it. Like table.sort, it does not return anything.

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to sort in descending order.

entries.name: ToString
entries.description: Converts a table into a string

args.name: tbl
args.description: The table to iterate over.

args.name: displayName
args.description: A name for the table.

args.name: niceFormatting
args.description: Adds new lines and tabs to the string.

returns.description: The table formatted as a string.

entries.name: Task
entries.description: A single AI task. Returned by [ai_task.New](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ai_task.New).

entries.name: Init
entries.description:

entries.name: timer
entries.description: The timer library is a very useful set of functions which allow you to run a function periodically or after a given delay.

entries.name: Adjust
entries.description: Adjusts a previously created ([timer.Create](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Create)) timer with the given identifier.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer to adjust.

args.name: delay
args.description: The delay interval in seconds. **Must be specified.**

args.name: repetitions
args.description: Repetitions. Use `0` for infinite or `nil` to keep previous value.

args.name: func
args.description: The new function. Use `nil` to keep previous value.

returns.description: `true` if succeeded.

entries.name: Check
entries.description: This function does nothing.
entries.deprecated: If you want to check if whether or not a timer exists, use timer.Exists.

entries.name: Create
entries.description:
Creates a new timer that will repeat its function given amount of times.
This function also requires the timer to be named, which allows you to control it after it was created via the [timer](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer).

For a simple one-time timer with no identifiers, see [timer.Simple](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Simple).

**WARNING**: Timers use [Global.CurTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CurTime) internally. Due to this, they won't advance while the client is timing out from the server or on an empty dedicated server due to hibernation. (unless `sv_hibernate_think` is set to `1` or `delay` is set to `0` ).

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer to create. Must be unique. If a timer already exists with the same identifier, that timer will be updated to the new settings and reset.

args.name: delay
args.description: The delay interval in seconds. If the delay is too small, the timer will fire on the next GM:Tick.

args.name: repetitions
args.description: The number of times to repeat the timer. Enter `0` or any value below `0` for infinite repetitions.

args.name: func
args.description: Function called when timer has finished the countdown.

entries.name: Destroy
entries.description: Stops and destroys the given timer. Alias of [timer.Remove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Remove).

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer to destroy.

entries.deprecated: You should be using timer.Remove instead.

entries.name: Exists
entries.description:
Returns whenever the given timer exists or not.

For debugging purposes you can use the following commands:
* `lua_dumptimers_cl`
* `lua_dumptimers_sv`
* `lua_dumptimers_menu`

These will list all active timers in each realm.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

returns.description: Returns true if the timer exists, false if it doesn't

entries.name: IsPaused
entries.description: Returns whenever the given timer is paused or not. ([timer.Pause](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Pause))

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer. (timer.Create)

returns.description: Returns true if the timer is paused, false if it isn't, `nil` if it doesn't exist.

entries.name: Pause
entries.description: Pauses the given timer.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

entries.name: Remove
entries.description:
Stops and removes a timer created by [timer.Create](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Create).
**WARNING**: The timers are removed in the next frame! Keep this in mind when storing identifiers in variables.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer to remove.

entries.name: RepsLeft
entries.description: Returns amount of repetitions/executions left before the timer destroys itself.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

returns.description: The amount of executions left.

entries.name: Simple
entries.description:
Creates a simple timer that runs the given function after a specified delay.

For a more advanced version that you can control after creation, see [timer.Create](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Create).

**WARNING**: Timers use [Global.CurTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CurTime) internally. Due to this, they won't advance while the client is timing out from the server or on an empty dedicated server due to hibernation. (unless `sv_hibernate_think` is set to `1`).


**WARNING**: A previous message on this page stated that a delay of 0 would run the function on the next tick. This was partially an invalid assumption, and the true behavior is dependent on where `timer.Simple(0, func)` is called relative to `GarrysMod::Lua::Libraries::Timer::DoSimpleTimers`.



- If called *before* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the same frame.

- If called *during* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the same frame. **Note that calling timer.Simple(0, func) recursively (ie. a function that calls **`timer.simple(0, itself)`**) can lead to a hang!**

- If called *after* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the next frame.

For more information on hook execution order, see [Lua Hooks Order](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Lua_Hooks_Order).

As of a commit on [2026.1.5](https://commits.facepunch.com/574654), simple timers are queued to the next frame.

As of a commit on [2026.1.8](https://commits.facepunch.com/575132), only timers with the same callback function are queued to the next frame. [Source](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/6668#issuecomment-3725044829)

args.name: delay
args.description: How long until the function should be ran (in seconds). A value of `0` differs in behavior, depending on where you're calling this function.

args.name: func
args.description: The function to run after the specified delay.

entries.name: Start
entries.description:
Restarts the given timer.

**WARNING**: Timers won't advance while the client is timing out from the server.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

entries.name: Stop
entries.description: Stops the given timer and rewinds it.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

entries.name: TimeLeft
entries.description:
Returns amount of time left (in seconds) before the timer executes its function.

**NOTE**: If the timer is paused, the amount will be negative.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

returns.description: The amount of time left (in seconds).

entries.name: Toggle
entries.description: Runs either [timer.Pause](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.Pause) or [timer.UnPause](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/timer.UnPause) based on the timer's current status.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

entries.name: UnPause
entries.description: Unpauses the timer.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Identifier of the timer.

entries.name: Tool
entries.description:
A list of functions available inside a Sandbox Toolgun tool.

You can find the hooks [here](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/TOOL_Hooks), and members [here](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/TOOL).

entries.name: TOOL
entries.description:
The **TOOL** table is used in Sandbox tool creation. You can find a list of callbacks on the  page and a list of methods on the  page. Do note that some of the fields below have no effect on server-side operations.

The tool information box drawn on the HUD while your tool is selected has 2 values that are set by [language.Add](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/language.Add).
* `tool.[tool mode].name` - The tool name (Note this is NOT the same as TOOL.Name)
* `tool.[tool mode].desc` - The tool description

Ensure that all tool file names are entirely lowercase.  Including capital letters can lead to unintended behavior.

fields.name: AddToMenu
fields.description: If set to false, the tool won't be added to the tool menu and players will have to access it by other means.

fields.name: Category
fields.description: The tool menu category under which the tool should be listed.

fields.name: Command
fields.description: The console command to execute upon being selected in the Q menu.

fields.name: Name
fields.description:
The name of the tool in the Q menu.
Common practice is to set this to "#tool.[lua filename].name" to match the name displayed in the tool information box.

fields.name: ClientConVar
fields.description:
A key-value ( convar name-default value ) table containing the client-side convars to create. All convars will be prefixed with the filename of the tool.
You can later use Tool:GetClientNumber or Tool:GetClientInfo to retrieve these values.

fields.name: ServerConVar
fields.description: Same as above, but created server-side instead.

fields.name: ClientConVars
fields.description: A key-value ( string name - ConVar object ) table containing the cached convar objected created from `ClientConVar`.

fields.name: ServerConVars
fields.description: Same as above, but server-side (`ServerConVar`) instead.

fields.name: BuildCPanel
fields.description:
The function that is called to build the context menu for your tool. It has one argument, namely the context menu's base panel to which all of your custom panels are going to be parented to.

While it might sound like a hook, it isn't - you won't receive a `self` argument inside the function. See TOOL.BuildCPanel.

fields.name: Information
fields.description:
Allows you to override the tool usage information shown when the tool is equipped.
See Tool Information Display for more information.

fields.name: Mode
fields.description:
Class name of the tool. (name of the .lua file)

This is set automatically.

fields.name: Tab
fields.description: The tool tab (spawnmenu.AddToolTab) to add this tool to. (The internal name, first argument)

fields.name: LeftClickAutomatic
fields.description: When enabled the game tries to run the left mouse click as soon as possible

fields.name: RightClickAutomatic
fields.description: When enabled the game tries to run the right mouse click as soon as possible

entries.name: TOOL
entries.description:
**NOTE**: This function or feature is only available in the Sandbox gamemode and its [derivatives](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.DeriveGamemode).


A list of hooks (or callbacks) that are available for you to override in a tool. This is only applicable to sandbox and sandbox-derived gamemodes.

See also: [Structures/TOOL](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/TOOL) and [Tool](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool).

entries.name: Allowed
entries.description:
Returns whether the tool is allowed to be used or not. This function ignores the [SANDBOX:CanTool](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/SANDBOX:CanTool) hook.

By default this will always return true clientside and uses `TOOL.AllowedCVar`which is a [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar) object pointing to  `toolmode_allow_*toolname*` convar on the server.

returns.description: Returns true if the tool is allowed.

entries.name: BuildConVarList
entries.description: Builds a list of all ConVars set via the ClientConVar variable on the [Structures/TOOL](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/TOOL) and their default values. This is used for the preset system.

returns.name: convars
returns.description: A list of all convars and their default values.

entries.name: CheckObjects
entries.description:
**INTERNAL**: This is called automatically for most toolgun actions so you shouldn't need to use it.


Checks all added objects to see if they're still valid, if not, clears the list of objects.

entries.name: ClearObjects
entries.description: Clears all objects previously set with [Tool:SetObject](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:SetObject).

entries.name: Create
entries.description:
**INTERNAL**: This is called automatically for all tools.

Initializes the tool object

returns.name: tool
returns.description: The created tool object.

entries.name: CreateConVars
entries.description:
**INTERNAL**: This is called automatically for all tools.


Creates clientside ConVars based on the ClientConVar table specified in the tool structure. Also creates the 'toolmode_allow_X' ConVar.

entries.name: Deploy
entries.description:
Called when [WEAPON:Deploy](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:Deploy) of the toolgun is called.

This is also called when switching from another tool on the server.

returns.description: Return true to allow switching away from the toolgun using lastinv command

entries.description: Called when [WEAPON:DrawHUD](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawHUD) of the toolgun is called, only when the user has this tool selected.

entries.name: DrawToolScreen
entries.description:
Called after the default tool screen has been drawn from [WEAPON:RenderScreen](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:RenderScreen).

**NOTE**: If this method exists on the TOOL object table, the default scrolling text will not be drawn

**NOTE**: Materials rendered in this hook require $ignorez parameter to draw properly.

args.description: The width of the tool's screen in pixels.

args.name: height
args.description: The height of the tool's screen in pixels.

entries.name: FreezeMovement
entries.description: Called when [WEAPON:Think](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:Think) of the toolgun is called, only when the user has this tool selected.

args.name: default
args.description: The default value to return in case the lookup fails.

returns.description: The value of the requested ConVar. It will be true if the value if the convar is not 0, just like ConVar:GetBool

args.name: name

returns.description: The value of the requested ConVar.

entries.description: Attempts to grab a clientside tool [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar)'s value as a [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number).

args.name: name

args.name: default

entries.name: SetObject
entries.description:
Stores an [Entity](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity) for later use in the tool.

The stored values can be retrieved by [Tool:GetEnt](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetEnt), [Tool:GetPos](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetPos), [Tool:GetLocalPos](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetLocalPos), [Tool:GetPhys](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetPhys), [Tool:GetBone](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetBone) and [Tool:GetNormal](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:GetNormal)

args.name: id
args.description: The id of the object to store.

args.name: ent
args.description: The entity to store.

args.name: pos
args.description:
The position to store.
this position is in **global space** and is internally converted to **local space** relative to the object, so when you retrieve it later it will be corrected to the object's new position

args.name: phys
args.description: The physics object to store.

args.name: bone
args.description: The hit bone to store.

args.name: normal
args.description: The hit normal to store.

entries.name: SetOperation
entries.description:
Sets the current operation of the tool. Does nothing clientside. See also [Tool:SetStage](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:SetStage).

Operations and stages work as follows:
* Operation 1
* * Stage 1
* * Stage 2
* * Stage 3
* Operation 2
* * Stage 1
* * Stage 2
* * Stage ...

args.name: operation
args.description: The new operation ID to set.

entries.name: UpdateGhostEntity
entries.description:
Updates the position and orientation of the ghost entity based on where the toolgun owner is looking along with data from object with id 1 set by [Tool:SetObject](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Tool:SetObject).

This should be called in the tool's [TOOL:Think](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/TOOL:Think) hook.

This command is only used for tools that move props, such as easy weld, axis and motor. If you want to update a ghost like the thruster tool does it for example, check its [source code](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/sandbox/entities/weapons/gmod_tool/stools/thruster.lua#L179).

entries.name: Trace
entries.description: Table structure used for [util.TraceLine](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TraceLine).

fields.name: start
fields.description: The start position of the trace

fields.name: endpos
fields.description: The end position of the trace

fields.name: filter
fields.description:
Things the trace should not hit. Can be an entity, a table of entities, a table of entity classes or a function:

	

Function argument(s):
* Entity `ent` - The entity that the trace hit

Function return value(s):
* boolean `undefined` - Return `true` to hit the entity, `false` to skip it.


	Using a function here is super slow. Try to avoid it.

arguments.name: ent
arguments.description: The entity that the trace hit

returns.description: Return `true` to hit the entity, `false` to skip it.

fields.name: mask
fields.description: The trace mask Enums/MASK. This determines what the trace should hit and what it shouldn't hit. A mask is a combination of Enums/CONTENTS - you can use these for more advanced masks.

fields.name: collisiongroup
fields.description: The collision group Enums/COLLISION_GROUP. This determines what the trace should hit in regards to the entity's collision group.

fields.name: ignoreworld
fields.description: Should the trace ignore world or not

fields.name: output
fields.description: If set, the trace result will be written to the supplied table instead of returning a new table

fields.name: whitelist
fields.description: Turns the `filter` field into a whitelist, if it is a table.

fields.name: hitclientonly
fields.description: Enables traces to hit clientside only entities. Keep in mind that most naturally spawned entities are classified as debris, so extra `mask` values might be required.

entries.description: Enumerations used by [Structures/AmmoData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/AmmoData).

items.description: Generates no tracer effects
Generates tracer effects
Unused.
Unused.
Generates tracer and makes whizzing noises if the bullet flies past the player being shot at

entries.name: TraceResult
entries.description:
Table structure used as trace result. Default values are when the trace hits nothing.

See [util.TraceLine](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TraceLine) and [util.TraceHull](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TraceHull).

fields.name: Entity
fields.description: The entity hit by the trace.

fields.name: Fraction
fields.description: This indicates the how much of your trace length was used from 0-1 (resultLength/originalLength).

fields.name: FractionLeftSolid
fields.description: Given the trace started in a solid enviroment, this will return at what distance the trace left the solid from 0-1. Doesn't work if the trace hit a non-worldspawn entity.

fields.name: Hit
fields.description: Indicates whether the trace hit something.

fields.name: HitBox
fields.description: The ID of the hitbox hit by the trace, or ID of the static prop hit in case of hitting the world.

fields.name: HitGroup
fields.description: Enums/HITGROUP describing what hitgroup the trace hit (not the same as HitBox).

fields.name: HitNoDraw
fields.description: Indicates whenever the trace hit a no-draw brush.

fields.name: HitNonWorld
fields.description: Indicates whenever the trace did not hit the world.

fields.name: HitNormal
fields.description: The direction of the surface that was hit as a normal vector (vector with Vector:Length of 1).

fields.name: HitPos
fields.description: The position the trace stopped. This will be the provided endpos if the trace hit nothing.

fields.name: HitSky
fields.description: Indicates whenever the trace hit the sky.

fields.name: HitTexture
fields.description: The surface material (not texture) of whatever the trace hit. Will be `**displacement**` if the trace hit a displacement, and `**studio**` if it hit a prop.

fields.name: HitWorld
fields.description: Indicates whenever the trace hit the world.

fields.name: MatType
fields.description: Enums/MAT of the material hit by the trace.

fields.name: Normal
fields.description:
The direction of the trace as a normal vector (vector with Vector:Length of 1).

Equivalent to: `( traceRes.HitPos - traceRes.StartPos ):Normalize()`

fields.name: PhysicsBone
fields.description:
The PhysObj ID that was hit.

Used for Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum.

fields.name: StartPos
fields.description: The origin of the trace. Will match the provided startpos.

fields.name: SurfaceProps
fields.description:
ID of hit surface property from `scripts/surfaceproperties.txt`.
You can get the name using util.GetSurfacePropName.

Used for CEffectData:SetSurfaceProp.

fields.name: StartSolid
fields.description: Indicates whenever the trace started in a solid enviroment.

fields.name: AllSolid
fields.description: True if the entire trace is inside a solid.

fields.name: SurfaceFlags
fields.description: The surface flags of the hit surface. See Enums/SURF.

fields.name: DispFlags
fields.description: The displacement flags of the hit surface. See Enums/DISPSURF.

fields.name: Contents
fields.description: The contents of the hit surface. See Enums/CONTENTS.

fields.name: HitBoxBone
fields.description: BoneID on the model that the hit hitbox is attached to, if available.

entries.name: UGCFileInfo
entries.description: Table structure used by [steamworks.FileInfo](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/steamworks.FileInfo).

fields.name: id
fields.description: The Workshop item ID

fields.name: title
fields.description: The title of the Workshop item

fields.name: description
fields.description: The description of the Workshop item. It will be limited to 255 characters (by Steam) unless steamworks.FileInfo is called with the `extraInfo` parameter set.

fields.name: fileid
fields.description: The internal File ID of the workshop item, if any

fields.name: previewid
fields.description: The internal File ID of the workshop item preview, if any

fields.name: previewurl
fields.description: A URL to the preview image of the workshop item

fields.name: owner
fields.description: The SteamID64 of the original uploader of the addon

fields.name: created
fields.description: Unix timestamp of when the item was created

fields.name: updated
fields.description: Unix timestamp of when the file was last updated

fields.name: banned
fields.description: Whether the file is banned or not

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Comma (,) separated list of tags, may be truncated to some length

fields.name: size
fields.description: File size of the workshop item contents in bytes

fields.name: previewsize
fields.description: Filesize of the preview file in bytes

fields.name: installed
fields.description: If the addon is subscribed, this value represents whether it is installed on the client and its files are accessible, false otherwise.

fields.name: disabled
fields.description: If the addon is subscribed, this value represents whether it is disabled on the client, false otherwise.

fields.name: children
fields.description:
A list of child Workshop Items for this item.

For collections this will be sub-collections, for workshop items this will be the items they depend on.

fields.name: ownername
fields.description:
We advise against using this. It may be changed or removed in a future update.

The "nice" name of the Uploader, or "Unnammed Player" if we failed to get the data for some reason.

Do not use this field as it will most likely not be updated in time. Use steamworks.RequestPlayerInfo instead.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
If this key is set, no other data will be present in the response.

Values above 0 represent Steam Error codes (https://steamerrors.com/), values below 0 mean the following:
* -1 means Failed to create query
* -2 means Failed to send query
* -3 means Received 0 or more than 1 result
* -4 means Failed to get item data from the response
* -5 means Workshop item ID in the response is invalid
* -6 means Workshop item ID in response is mismatching the requested file ID

fields.name: up
fields.description: Number of "up" votes for this item.

fields.name: down
fields.description: Number of "down" votes for this item.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Number of total votes (up and down) for this item. This is NOT `up - down`.

fields.name: score
fields.description: The up down vote ratio for this item, i.e. `1` is when every vote is `up`, `0.5` is when half of the total votes are the up votes, etc.

fields.name: content_descriptors
fields.description:
A list of Steam content descriptiors for this Steam Workshop item.

Possible values are:
* `general_mature`
* `gore`
* `suggestive`
* `nudity`
* `adult_only`

fields.name: extra_previews
fields.description:
If present, a list of additional previews for this Workshop item.

steamworks.FileInfo must be called with `extraInfo` parameter.

It will be a table of tables with the following keys:
* number `type` - type of additional preview. 0 = is normal image, 1=YouTube video ID
* string `url` - URL to the additional preview. Format depends on the type.

entries.name: utf8
entries.description:
The utf8 library provides basic support for UTF-8 encoding. This library does not provide any support for Unicode other than the handling of the encoding. Any operation that needs the meaning of a character, such as character classification, is outside its scope.

Unless stated otherwise, all functions that expect a byte position as a parameter assume that the given position is either the start of a byte sequence or one plus the length of the subject string. As in the string library, negative indices count from the end of the string.

entries.name: char
entries.description: Receives zero or more integers, converts each one to its corresponding UTF-8 byte sequence and returns a string with the concatenation of all these sequences.

args.name: codepoints
args.description: Unicode code points to be converted in to a UTF-8 string.

returns.description: UTF-8 string generated from given arguments.

entries.name: codepoint
entries.description: Returns the codepoints (as numbers) from all characters in the given string that start between byte position startPos and endPos. It raises an error if it meets any invalid byte sequence. This functions similarly to [string.byte](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string.byte).

args.name: string
args.description: The string that you will get the code(s) from.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The starting byte of the string to get the codepoint of.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The ending byte of the string to get the codepoint of.

returns.description: The codepoint number(s).

entries.name: codes
entries.description: Returns an iterator (like [string.gmatch](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string.gmatch)) which returns both the position and codepoint of each utf8 character in the string. It raises an error if it meets any invalid byte sequence.

args.name: string
args.description: The string that you will get the codes from.

returns.description: The iterator (to be used in a for loop).

entries.name: force
entries.description:
Forces a string to contain only valid UTF-8 data. Invalid sequences are replaced with U+FFFD (the Unicode replacement character).

This is a lazy way for users to ensure a string contains only valid UTF-8 data.

args.name: string
args.description: The string that will become a valid UTF-8 string.

returns.description: The UTF-8 string.

entries.name: GetChar
entries.description: A UTF-8 compatible version of [string.GetChar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string.GetChar).

args.name: str
args.description: The string that you will be searching with the supplied index.

args.name: index
args.description: The index's value of the string to be returned.

returns.description: str

entries.name: len
entries.description: Returns the number of UTF-8 sequences in the given string between positions startPos and endPos (both inclusive). If it finds any invalid UTF-8 byte sequence, returns false as well as the position of the first invalid byte.

args.name: string
args.description: The string to calculate the length of.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The starting position to get the length from.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The ending position to get the length from.

returns.description: The number of UTF-8 characters in the string. If there are invalid bytes, this will be false.
The position of the first invalid byte. If there were no invalid bytes, this will be nil.

entries.name: offset
entries.description: Returns the byte-index of the n'th UTF-8-character after the given startPos (nil if none). startPos defaults to 1 when n is positive and -1 when n is negative. If n is zero, this function instead returns the byte-index of the UTF-8-character startPos lies within.

args.name: string
args.description: The string that you will get the byte position from.

args.name: n
args.description: The position to get the beginning byte position from.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The offset for n.

returns.description: Starting byte-index of the given position.

A UTF-8 compatible version of [string.sub](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string.sub).
	**WARNING**: Avoid using this function on large strings every tick/frame, as it may cause lags.

args.name: string

args.name: StartPos

entries.name: AddNetworkString
entries.description:
Adds the specified string to a string table, which will cache it and network it to all clients automatically.
Whenever you want to create a net message with [net.Start](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/net.Start), you must add the name of that message as a networked string via this function.

If the passed string already exists, nothing will happen and the ID of the existing item will be returned.

**NOTE**: Each unique network name needs to be pooled once - do not put this function call into any other functions if you're using a constant string. Preferable place for this function is in a serverside lua file, or in a shared file with the [net.Receive](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/net.Receive) function.

The string table used for this function does not interfere with the engine string tables and has 4095 slots.  
This limit is shared among all entities, SetNW* and SetGlobal* functions. If you exceed the limit, you cannot create new variables, and you will get the following warning:
```lua 
Warning:  Table networkstring is full, can't add [key]
```
**WARNING**: Existing variables will still get updated without the warning. You can check the limit by counting up until [util.NetworkIDToString](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.NetworkIDToString) returns nil

args.name: str
args.description: Adds the specified string to the string table.

returns.description:
The id of the string that was added to the string table.
Same as calling util.NetworkStringToID.

entries.name: Compress
entries.description:
Compresses the given string using the [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm.

Use with [net.WriteData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/net.WriteData) and [net.ReadData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/net.ReadData) for networking and  [util.Decompress](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Decompress) to decompress the data.

**NOTE**: The output of this function will have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L56-L63)

You may therefore experience issues using the output of this function **_outside of Garry's Mod_**. If you need to do this, you will need to manually strip the first 8 bytes from the compressed output, or use third-party tools such as [gmod-lzma](https://github.com/WilliamVenner/gmod-lzma-rs) to decompress the output instead.

args.name: str
args.description: String to compress.

returns.description: The compressed string, or an empty string if the input string was zero length ("").

entries.name: CRC
entries.description:
Generates the [CRC Checksum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclic_redundancy_check) of the specified string.
		
		**WARNING**: This is NOT a hashing function. It is a checksum, typically used for error detection/data corruption detection. It is possible for this function to generate "collisions", where two different strings will produce the same CRC. If you need a hashing function, use [util.SHA256](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.SHA256).

args.name: stringToChecksum
args.description: The string to calculate the checksum of.

returns.description: The unsigned 32 bit checksum.

entries.name: Decompress
entries.description:
Decompresses the given string using [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm. Used to decompress strings previously compressed with [util.Compress](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Compress).

**WARNING**: When reading user data, always try to specify `maxSize` argument, otherwise the server can be [decompression bombed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zip_bomb) with bad data that will fill up all Lua memory

**NOTE**: This function expects the compressed input data to have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L101)

If your compressed input data was compressed by [util.Compress](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Compress), you don't need to worry about this - the uncompressed size of the data is already prepended to its output.

However, if your compressed data was produced using standard tools **_outside of Garry's Mod_**, you will need to manually prepend the length of the uncompressed data to its compressed form as an 8-byte little endian integer.

args.name: compressedString
args.description: The compressed string to decompress.

args.name: maxSize
args.description: The maximum size of uncompressed data in bytes, if greater it fails.

returns.description: The original, decompressed string or `nil` on failure or invalid input. Also returns empty string if the input string was zero length ("").

Creates an effect with the specified data.

For Orange Box `.pcf` particles, see [Global.ParticleEffect](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.ParticleEffect), [Global.ParticleEffectAttach](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.ParticleEffectAttach) and  [Global.CreateParticleSystem](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystem).

	**NOTE**: When dispatching an effect from the server, some values may be clamped for networking optimizations. Visit the Set accessors on [CEffectData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/CEffectData) to see which ones are affected.

You will need to couple this function with [Global.IsFirstTimePredicted](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.IsFirstTimePredicted) if you want to use it in a [predicted hook](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Prediction).

args.name: effectName

The name of the effect to create.

You can find a list of Default_Effects. You can create your own in LUA, [example effects can be found here](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/tree/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/sandbox/entities/effects) and [here](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/tree/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/base/entities/effects).

	
If you use this function with Lua effects more than 2048 times in a single frame,   

you will get errors: `Broke possible Lua Effect creation infinite loop` and `Too many Lua Effects (2049)! Are you killing them properly?`.

**NOTE**: In some cases, especially in a chatbox, messages from some players may return an empty string if the context argument used for filtering is `TEXT_FILTER_CHAT` and [if the local player has blocked the sender of the message on Steam](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/5161#issuecomment-1035153941).

entries.name: GetUserGroups

entries.name: IsValidModel
entries.description:
Checks if the specified model is valid.
 

A model is considered invalid in following cases:
* Starts with a space or **maps**
* Doesn't start with **models**
* Contains any of the following:
  * `_gestures`
  * `_animations`
  * `_postures`
  * `_gst`
  * `_pst`
  * `_shd`
  * `_ss`
  * `_anm`
  * `.bsp`
  * `cs_fix`
* If the model isn't precached on the server, AND if the model file doesn't exist on disk
* If precache failed
* Model is the error model

Running this function will also precache the model.

args.name: modelName
args.description: Name/Path of the model to check.

returns.description: Whether the model is valid or not. Returns false clientside if the model is not precached by the server.

entries.description: Checks whether the given numbered physics object of the given entity is valid or not. Most useful for ragdolls.

args.name: ent
args.description: The entity to take.

args.name: physobj
args.description: Number of the physics object to test.

returns.description: `true` that's valid, `false` otherwise.

entries.name: IsValidProp
entries.description: Checks if the specified prop is valid (has valid physics object).

args.name: modelName
args.description: Name/Path of the model to check.

returns.description: Returns true if the specified prop is valid; otherwise false.

entries.name: IsValidRagdoll
entries.description: Checks if the specified model name points to a valid ragdoll.

args.name: ragdollName
args.description: Name/Path of the ragdoll model to check.

returns.description: Returns true if the specified model name points to a valid ragdoll; otherwise false.

entries.name: JSONToTable
entries.description:
Converts a JSON string to a Lua table. It supports comments and trailing commas.

See [util.TableToJSON](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TableToJSON) for the opposite function.

Colors will not have the color metatable.

args.name: json
args.description: The JSON string to convert.

args.name: ignoreLimits
args.description:
ignore the depth and breadth limits, **use at your own risk!**.
			If this is false, there is a limit of 15,000 keys total.

args.name: ignoreConversions
args.description:
ignore string to number conversions for table keys.
			
				if this is false, keys are converted to numbers wherever possible. This means using [Player:SteamID64](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SteamID64) as keys won't work.

returns.description: The table containing converted information. Returns `nil` on failure.

entries.name: KeyValuesToTable
entries.description:
Converts a Valve KeyValue string (typically from [util.TableToKeyValues](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TableToKeyValues)) to a Lua table.

**NOTE**: Due to how [table](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/table)s work in Lua, keys will not repeat within a table. See [util.KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder) for alternative.

args.name: keyValues
args.description: The KeyValue string to convert.

args.name: usesEscapeSequences
args.description: If set to true, will replace `\t`, `\n`, `\"` and `\\` in the input text with their escaped variants

args.name: preserveKeyCase
args.description: Whether we should preserve key case (may fail) or not (always lowercase)

returns.description: The converted table

entries.name: KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder
entries.description: Similar to [util.KeyValuesToTable](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.KeyValuesToTable), but it also preserves order of keys (since Lua dictionary-style tables do not guarantee a specific order), and allows handling of repeated keys. (since each key can only appear once in a dictionary data structure)

args.name: keyValues
args.description: The Valve KeyValue formatted text.

args.name: usesEscapeSequences
args.description: If set to true, will replace `\t`, `\n`, `\"` and `\\` in the input text with their escaped variants

args.name: preserveKeyCase
args.description: Whether we should preserve key case (may fail) or not (always lowercase)

returns.description: The output table

If that specific physics object is valid, then PhysObj:LocalToWorld is used.

entries.name: ParticleTracer
entries.description:
Creates an orange box (.pcf) tracer effect with the given parameters. See [util.ParticleTracerEx](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.ParticleTracerEx) for version with additional arguments.

Internally uses `ParticleTracer` engine effect. ([util.Effect](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Effect)) which then spawns in `ParticleEffect` effect.
**NOTE**: The default bullet effect is not in .pcf format, therefore it is not used with util.ParticleTracer.  Consider utilizing [util.Effect](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Effect) instead

args.name: name
args.description:
The name of the .pcf particle effect to use for the tracer.

Control Point 0 is the start location. Control Point 1 is the end pos.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The start position of the tracer.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The end position of the tracer.

args.name: doWhiz
args.description: Whether to play the hit near-miss (whiz) sound.

entries.name: ParticleTracerEx
entries.description: Creates a tracer effect with the given parameters. Expanded version of [util.ParticleTracer](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.ParticleTracer).

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the tracer effect.

args.name: startPos
args.description: The start position of the tracer.

args.name: endPos
args.description: The end position of the tracer.

args.name: doWhiz
args.description: Play the hit miss(whiz) sound.

args.name: entityIndex
args.description: Entity index of the emitting entity.

args.name: attachmentIndex
args.description: Attachment index to be used as origin.

entries.name: PixelVisible
entries.description:
Returns the visibility of a square that is always pointed at the camera in the world-space.

This is typically used for in-game sprites or "billboards". ([render.DrawSprite](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.DrawSprite))

args.name: position
args.description: The center of the visibility test.

args.name: size
args.description: The size of the square to check for visibility.

args.name: PixVis
args.description:
The PixVis handle created with util.GetPixelVisibleHandle.
		Don't use the same handle twice per tick or it will give unpredictable results.

returns.description: Visibility percentage, in range of `[0-1]`. `0` when none of the area is visible, `0.5` when half the area is visible, `1` when all of it is visible, etc.

entries.name: PointContents
entries.description:
Returns the contents of the position specified.
		**NOTE**: This function will sample only the world environments. It can be used to check if [Entity:GetPos](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetPos) is underwater for example unlike [Entity:WaterLevel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:WaterLevel) which works for players only.

args.name: position
args.description: Position to get the contents sample from.

returns.description: Contents bitflag, see Enums/CONTENTS

entries.name: PrecacheModel
entries.description:
Precaches a model for later use. Model is cached after being loaded once.
		**WARNING**: Modelprecache is limited to 8192 unique models. When it reaches the limit the game will crash.


		**NOTE**: Does nothing on the client.

args.name: modelName
args.description: The model to precache.

entries.name: PrecacheSound
entries.description:
Precaches a sound for later use. Sound is cached after being loaded once.
**NOTE**: Soundcache is limited to 16384 unique sounds on the server. Due to this fact this function is disabled on purpose, as exceeding the limit causes the server to shutdown.


Ultimately does nothing on client, and only works with sound scripts, not direct paths.

args.name: soundName
args.description: The sound to precache.

entries.name: QuickTrace
entries.description:
Performs a trace with the given origin, direction, and filter.
**NOTE**: This function will throw an error in the menu realm because it internally uses util.TraceLine which doesn't exist in the menu realm and thus error.

args.name: origin
args.description: The origin of the trace.

args.name: dir
args.description: The direction of the trace times the distance of the trace. This is added to the origin to determine the endpos.

args.name: filter
args.description: Entity which should be ignored by the trace. Can also be a table of entities or a function - see Structures/Trace.

returns.description: Trace result. See Structures/TraceResult.

entries.name: RelativePathToFull_Menu
entries.description:
Converts the relative path of a given file to the full path on disk.  
		You can use [util.FullPathToRelative_Menu](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.FullPathToRelative_Menu) to convert the full path back to the relative path.

args.name: mountPath
args.description: The path to look for the files and directories in. See File_Search_Paths for a list of valid paths.

returns.name: fullpath
returns.description: The full path to the file.

entries.name: RelativePathToGMA_Menu
entries.description: Returns which Workshop addon the given file belongs to.

args.name: filePath

returns.name: addonInfo
