The info about owner addon. Will return nil if the file doesn't belong to an addon. Table Structure:
```lua
Author	=	[Addon Author]
File	=	[Steam folder]\workshop\content\4000\[Addon ID]/[GMA Name].gma
ID	=	[Addon ID]
Title	=	[Addon Title]
```

entries.name: RemoveDecalsAt
entries.description: Removes world decals at given position, in given radius. Does not remove decals on models!

args.name: pos
args.description: The position at which to remove decals.

args.name: distance
args.description: Radius of the sphere to remove decals in.

args.name: limit
args.description: If set to above 0, only remove this many decals.

args.name: permanent
args.description:
Whether to remove map-spawned decals (`true`), or only gameplay-spawned decals 
 such as bullet holes or anything placed by util.Decal and similar(`false`)

returns.name: removed
returns.description: How many decals were removed.

entries.name: RemovePData
entries.description:
Removes persistent data of an offline player using their SteamID.

See also [Player:RemovePData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:RemovePData) for a more convenient version of this function for online players, [util.SetPData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.SetPData) and 
 [util.GetPData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.GetPData) for the other accompanying functions.

**NOTE**: This function internally uses [util.SteamIDTo64](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.SteamIDTo64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which can cause collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry). This function now tries to remove both old and new entries.

args.name: steamID
args.description: SteamID of the player to remove data of, in the `STEAM_0:0:0` format. See Player:SteamID.

args.name: name
args.description: Variable name to remove

entries.name: ScreenShake
entries.description:
Makes the screen shake.

**NOTE**: The screen shake effect is rendered by modifying the view origin on the client. If you override the view origin in [GM:CalcView](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:CalcView) you may not be able to see the shake effect.

args.name: pos
args.description:
The origin of the effect.
			
Used serverside only, to determine which clients the event should be networked to.

args.name: amplitude
args.description: The strength of the effect. How far away from its origin the camera will move while shaking.

args.name: frequency
args.description: How many times per second to change the direction of the camera wobble. 40 is generally enough; values higher are hardly distinguishable.

args.name: duration
args.description: The duration of the effect in seconds.

args.name: radius
args.description:
The range from the origin within which views will be affected, in Hammer units.

This is used when networking the event to clients only.

args.name: airshake
args.description:
Whether players in the air should also be affected.

Used serverside only to determine which clients to send the event to.

args.name: filter
args.description: If set, will only network the screen shake event to players present in the filter.

entries.name: SetPData
entries.description:
Sets persistent data for offline player using their SteamID.

See also [Player:SetPData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SetPData) for a more convenient version of this function for online players, [util.RemovePData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.RemovePData) and 
 [util.GetPData](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.GetPData) for the other accompanying functions.
**NOTE**: This function internally uses [util.SteamIDTo64](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.SteamIDTo64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which could have caused collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry).

args.name: steamID
args.description: SteamID of the player, in the `STEAM_0:0:0` format. See Player:SteamID.

args.name: name
args.description: Variable name to store the value in.

args.name: value
args.description: The value to store.

entries.name: SHA1
entries.description:
Generates the [SHA-1 hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1) of the specified string.
		**WARNING**: SHA-1 is considered cryptographically broken and is known to be vulnerable to a variety of attacks. If security is a concern, use [util.SHA256](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.SHA256).

args.name: stringToHash
args.description: The string to calculate the SHA-1 hash of.

returns.description: The SHA-1 hash of the string in hexadecimal form.

entries.name: SHA256
entries.description: Generates the [SHA-256 hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) of the specified string. This is mostly unique and is astronomically unlikely to return the same hash for a different string unlike [util.CRC](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.CRC) or [util.MD5](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.MD5) which are both much more vulnerable to duplicate returns.

args.name: stringToHash
args.description: The string to calculate the SHA-256 hash of.

returns.description: The SHA-256 hash of the string in hexadecimal form.

entries.name: SharedRandom
entries.description:
Generates a random float value that should be the same on client and server.

**NOTE**: This function is best used in a [predicted hook](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/prediction).


This uses a different method of obtaining random numbers and is unaffected by [math.randomseed](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/math.randomseed). Instead it uses an internal seed that is based on the player's current predicted command and is fixed to a value of -1 outside of prediction.

args.name: uniqueName

A timer object. It has the following methods:
* `Reset()` - Resets and stops the timer.

entries.name: TraceHull
entries.description:
Performs an AABB hull (axis-aligned bounding box, aka not rotated) trace with the given trace data.

This trace type cannot hit hitboxes.

See [util.TraceLine](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TraceLine) for a simple line ("ray") trace.

**NOTE**: This function may not always give desired results clientside due to certain physics mechanisms not existing on the client. Use it serverside for accurate results.

returns.description: Trace result. See Structures/TraceResult

entries.name: TraceLine
entries.description:
Performs an infinitely thin, invisible ray trace (or "trace") in a line from a starting point to an ending point and returns a table of information about what, if anything, the trace line hit or intersected.

Traces intersect with the physics meshes of [solid](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/enums/SOLID), [server-side](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/States), [entities](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity) (including the [game world](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/game.GetWorld)) but cannot detect client-side only entities unless [hitclientonly](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/Trace#hitclientonly) is set to `true`.
  
See [ents.FindAlongRay](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ents.FindAlongRay) if you wish for the trace to not stop on first intersection.  
See [util.TraceHull](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.TraceHull) for a "box" type trace.

Traces do not differentiate between the inside and the outside faces of physics meshes. Because of this, if a trace starts within a solid physics mesh it will hit the inside faces of the physics mesh and may return unexpected values as a result.


You can use `r_visualizetraces` set to `1` (requires `sv_cheats` set to `1`) to visualize traces in real time for debugging purposes.

args.name: traceConfig
args.description: A table of data that configures the trace. See Structures/Trace for available options.

returns.description:
A table of information detailing where and what the trace line intersected, or `nil` if the trace is being done before the GM:InitPostEntity hook.

			For the table's format and available options see the Structures/TraceResult page.

entries.name: Vector
entries.description:
List of all possible functions to manipulate vectors.

Created by [Global.Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Vector).

 Type   | Name           | Description                    
 ------ | -------------- | ------------------------------ 
 [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) | `x`, `X`, `r` or `1` | The X component of the vector. 
 [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) | `y`, `Y`, `g` or `2` | The Y component of the vector. 
 [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) | `z`, `Z`, `b` or `3` | The Z component of the vector.

Metamethod | Second Operand | Description
---------- | -------------- | -----------
`__add` | [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of addition.
`__div` | [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) or [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of division.
`__eq` | [any](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/any) | Compares 2 operands, if they both are [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector), compares each individual component.
`__index` | [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) or [string](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string) | Gets the component of the [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector). Returns a [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number).
`__mul` | [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) or [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector)| Returns new [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of multiplication.
`__newindex` | [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) or [string](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string) | Sets the component of the [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector). Accepts [number](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/number) and [string](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string).
`__sub` | [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of subtraction.
`__tostring` | | Returns `x y z`.
`__unm` | | Returns new [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of negation.

entries.name: Add
entries.description: Adds the values of the argument vector to the original vector. This function is the same as vector1 + vector2 without creating a new vector object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

entries.name: AngleEx
entries.description: Returns the angle of this vector (normalized), but instead of assuming that up is [Global.Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Vector)( 0, 0, 1 ) (Like [Vector:Angle](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Angle) does) you can specify which direction is 'up' for the angle.

args.name: up

entries.name: Cross
entries.description:
Calculates the cross product of this vector and the passed one.

The cross product of two vectors is a 3-dimensional vector with a direction perpendicular (at right angles) to both of them (according to the [right-hand rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-hand_rule)), and magnitude equal to the area of parallelogram they span. This is defined as the product of the magnitudes, the sine of the angle between them, and unit (normal) vector `n` defined by the right-hand rule:
:**a** × **b** = |**a**| |**b**| sin(θ) **n̂**
where **a** and **b** are vectors, and **n̂** is a unit vector (magnitude of 1) perpendicular to both.

args.name: otherVector
args.description: Vector to calculate the cross product with.

returns.description: The cross product of the two vectors.

entries.name: Distance
entries.description:
Returns the Euclidean distance between the vector and the other vector.

**NOTE**: This function is more expensive than [Vector:DistToSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:DistToSqr). However, please see the notes for [Vector:DistToSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:DistToSqr) before using it as squared distances are not the same as euclidean distances.

args.name: otherVector
args.description: The vector to get the distance to.

returns.description: Distance between the vectors.

entries.name: Distance2D
entries.description:
Returns the Euclidean distance between the vector and the other vector in 2D space. The Z axis is ignored.

**NOTE**: This function is more expensive than [Vector:Distance2DSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance2DSqr). However, please see the notes for [Vector:Distance2DSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance2DSqr) before using it as squared distances are not the same as Euclidean distances.

args.name: otherVector
args.description: The vector to get the distance to.

returns.description: Distance between the vectors in 2D space.

entries.name: Distance2DSqr
entries.description:
Returns the squared distance between 2 vectors in 2D space, ignoring the Z axis. This is faster than [Vector:Distance2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance2D) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.

	**NOTE**: Squared distances should not be summed. If you need to sum distances, use [Vector:Distance2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance2D).

When performing a distance check, ensure the distance being checked against is squared.

args.name: otherVec
args.description: The vector to calculate the distance to.

returns.description: Squared distance to the vector in 2D space.

entries.name: DistToSqr
entries.description:
Returns the squared distance of 2 vectors, this is quicker to call than [Vector:Distance](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance) as DistToSqr does not need to calculate the square root, which is an expensive process.

	**NOTE**: Squared distances should not be summed. If you need to sum distances, use [Vector:Distance](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Distance).

When performing a distance check, ensure the distance being checked against is squared. See example code below.

args.name: otherVec
args.description: The vector to calculate the distance to.

returns.description: Squared distance to the vector.

entries.name: Div
entries.description: Divide the vector by the given number, that means x, y and z are divided by that value. This will change the value of the original vector, see example 2 for division without changing the value.

args.name: divisor
args.description: The value to divide the vector with.

entries.name: Dot
entries.description:
Returns the [dot product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_product#Geometric_definition)  of this vector and the passed one.

The dot product of two vectors is the product of their magnitudes (lengths), and the cosine of the angle between them:
**a · b** = |**a**| |**b**| cos(θ) 
where **a** and **b** are vectors.
See [Vector:Length](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Length) for obtaining magnitudes.

A dot product returns just the cosine of the angle if both vectors are normalized, and zero if the vectors are at right angles to each other.

args.name: otherVector
args.description: The vector to calculate the dot product with

returns.description: The dot product between the two vectors

entries.name: DotProduct
entries.description: Returns the dot product of the two vectors.

args.name: Vector
args.description: The other vector.

returns.description: Dot Product

entries.deprecated: This is an alias of Vector:Dot. Use that instead.

entries.name: GetNegated
entries.description:
Returns the negative version of this vector, i.e. a vector with every component to the negative value of itself.

See also [Vector:Negate](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Negate).

returns.description: The negative of this vector.

entries.name: GetNormal
entries.description: Returns a normalized version of the vector. This is a alias of [Vector:GetNormalized](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:GetNormalized).

returns.description: Normalized version of the vector.

entries.deprecated: Use Vector:GetNormalized instead.

entries.name: GetNormalized
entries.description:
Returns a normalized version of the vector. Normalized means vector with same direction but with length of 1.

This does not affect the vector you call it on; to do this, use [Vector:Normalize](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Normalize).

entries.name: IsZero

entries.name: Length
entries.description:
Returns the [Euclidean length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_vector#Length) of the vector: √(x² + y² + z²).

		**WARNING**: This is a relatively expensive process since it uses the square root. It is recommended that you use [Vector:LengthSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:LengthSqr) whenever possible.

returns.description: Length of the vector.

entries.name: Length2D
entries.description:
Returns the length of the vector in two dimensions, without the Z axis.

		**WARNING**: This is a relatively expensive process since it uses the square root. It is recommended that you use [Vector:Length2DSqr](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Length2DSqr) whenever possible.

returns.description: Length of the vector in two dimensions, √(x² + y²)

entries.name: Length2DSqr
entries.description:
Returns the squared length of the vectors x and y value, x² + y².

This is faster than [Vector:Length2D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Length2D) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.

returns.description: Squared length of the vector in two dimensions

entries.name: LengthSqr
entries.description:
Returns the squared length of the vector, x² + y² + z².

This is faster than [Vector:Length](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector:Length) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.

returns.description: Squared length of the vector

entries.description:
Returns where on the screen the specified position vector would appear. A related function is [gui.ScreenToVector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/gui.ScreenToVector), which converts a 2D coordinate to a 3D direction.

**NOTE**: Should be called from a 3D rendering environment or after [cam.Start3D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start3D) or it may not work correctly.


Errors in a render hook can make this value incorrect until the player restarts their game.

[cam.Start3D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start3D) or 3D context [cam.Start](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start) with non-default parameters incorrectly sets the reference FOV for this function, causing incorrect return values. This can be fixed by creating and ending a default 3D context ([cam.Start3D](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/cam.Start3D) with no arguments).

Example usage in defined a custom spawnable vehicle:

list.Set( "Vehicles", "Jeep", {

	Class = "prop_vehicle_jeep_old",

fields.name: offcenter
fields.description:
This allows you to "zoom in" on a part of the screen - for example, the top-left quarter of the screen. This is similar to how [poster splits the screen](https://garry.blog/poster-screenshots/) into separate renders.

It's a table with 4 keys, controlling what portion of the screen to draw:
* left - where the left edge starts. Natural value is 0.
* right - where the right edge ends. Natural value is equal to w (the width of the viewport).
* top - where the `bottom` edge starts. Natural value is 0.
* bottom - where the `top` edge ends. Natural value is equal to h (the height of the viewport).

Note that top and bottom are reversed.

Values outside the viewport are allowed, but not recommended - instead you should increase the view FOV.

fields.description: Whether `m_bRenderToSubrectOfLargerScreen` if set for this view.

fields.name: offcenter
fields.description:
It's a table with 4 keys, controlling what portion of the screen to draw:
* left - where the left edge starts. Natural value is 0.
* right - where the right edge ends. Natural value is equal to w (the width of the viewport).
* top - where the `bottom` edge starts. Natural value is 0.
* bottom - where the `top` edge ends. Natural value is equal to h (the height of the viewport).

Note that top and bottom are reversed.

This will not be present if offscreen rendering is not enabled for this view.

See Structures/ViewData for more info.

entries.name: VMatrix
entries.description:
A 4x4 matrix.

This page lists all possible functions to manipulate matrices.

This object can be created by [Global.Matrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Matrix).

Metamethod | Second Operand | Description
---------- | -------------- | -----------
`__add` | [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) | Returns new [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of addition.
`__eq` | [any](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/any) | Compares 2 operands, if they both are [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix), compares each individual component.
`__mul` | [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) or [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) or [Vector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector) with the result of multiplication.
`__sub` | [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) | Returns new [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of subtraction.
`__tostring` |  | Returns a [string](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string) in format `[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]`.
`__unm` | | Returns new [VMatrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of negation.

entries.name: Add
entries.description: Adds given matrix to this matrix.

args.name: input
args.description: The input matrix to add.

entries.name: GetAngles
entries.description: Returns the absolute rotation of the matrix. Scaled matrix might produce unexpected results!

returns.description: Absolute rotation of the matrix

entries.name: GetField
entries.description: Returns a specific field in the matrix.

args.name: row
args.description: Row of the field whose value is to be retrieved, from 1 to 4

args.name: column
args.description: Column of the field whose value is to be retrieved, from 1 to 4

returns.description: The value of the specified field

entries.name: GetForward
entries.description:
Gets the forward direction of the matrix.

ie. The first column of the matrix, excluding the w coordinate.

returns.description: The forward direction of the matrix.

entries.name: GetInverse
entries.description:
Returns an inverted matrix without modifying the original matrix.

Inverting the matrix will fail if its [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) is 0 or close to 0. (ie. its "scale" in any direction is 0.)

See also [VMatrix:GetInverseTR](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix:GetInverseTR).

returns.description: The inverted matrix if possible, nil otherwise

entries.name: GetInverseTR
entries.description:
Returns an inverted matrix without modifying the original matrix. This function will not fail, but only works correctly on matrices that contain only translation and/or rotation.

Using this function on a matrix with modified scale may return an incorrect inverted matrix.

To get the inverse of a matrix that contains other modifications, see [VMatrix:GetInverse](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix:GetInverse).

returns.description: The inverted matrix.

entries.name: GetRight
entries.description:
Gets the right direction of the matrix.

ie. The second column of the matrix, negated, excluding the w coordinate.

returns.description: The right direction of the matrix.

entries.name: GetScale
entries.description: Returns the absolute scale of the matrix.

returns.description: Absolute scale of the matrix

entries.name: GetTranslation
entries.description: Returns the absolute translation of the matrix.

returns.description: Absolute translation of the matrix

entries.name: GetTransposed
entries.description: Returns the transpose (each row becomes a column) of this matrix.

returns.name: transposed
returns.description: The transposed matrix.

entries.name: GetUp
entries.description:
Gets the up direction of the matrix.

ie. The third column of the matrix, excluding the w coordinate.

returns.description: The up direction of the matrix.

entries.name: Identity
entries.description: Initializes the matrix as Identity matrix.

entries.name: Invert
entries.description:
Inverts the matrix.

Inverting the matrix will fail if its [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) is 0 or close to 0. (ie. its "scale" in any direction is 0.)

If the matrix cannot be inverted, it does not get modified.

See also [VMatrix:InvertTR](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix:InvertTR).

returns.description: Whether the matrix was inverted or not

entries.name: InvertTR
entries.description:
Quickly inverts the matrix. This function will not fail, but only works correctly on matrices that contain only translation and/or rotation.

Using this function on a matrix with modified scale may return an incorrect inverted matrix.

To invert a matrix that contains other modifications, see [VMatrix:Invert](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix:Invert). This function is faster.

entries.name: IsIdentity
entries.description: Returns whether the matrix is equal to Identity matrix or not.

returns.description: Is the matrix an Identity matrix or not

entries.name: IsRotationMatrix
entries.description:
Returns whether the matrix is a rotation matrix or not.

Technically it checks if the forward, right and up vectors are orthogonal and normalized.

returns.description: Is the matrix a rotation matrix or not

entries.name: IsZero
entries.description: Checks whenever all fields of the matrix are 0, aka if this is a [null matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_matrix).

returns.description: If the matrix is a null matrix.

args.name: input

Rotates the matrix by the given angle.

Postmultiplies the matrix by a rotation matrix (A = AR).

args.name: rotation
args.description: Rotation.

Scales the matrix by the given vector.

Postmultiplies the matrix by a scaling matrix (A = AS).

args.name: scale

entries.description:
Sets the up direction of the matrix.

ie. The third column of the matrix, excluding the w coordinate.

args.name: up

args.name: input
args.description: The input matrix to subtract.

entries.name: ToTable
entries.description: Converts the matrix to a 4x4 table. See [Global.Matrix](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.Matrix) function.

returns.description: The 4x4 table.

entries.name: Translate

Translates the matrix by the given vector aka. adds the vector to the translation.

entries.description:
Sets all components of the matrix to 0, also known as a [null matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_matrix).

This function is more efficient than setting each element manually.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.description:
This is a list of all methods only available for weapons. It is also possible to call [Entity](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity) functions on weapons.

**NOTE**: A list of available methods has been expanded in your navigation bar.

entries.name: WEAPON
entries.description:
Default weapon methods, that are available for use in SWEPs. These hooks **will not work** on non-scripted weapons, such as the Half-Life 2 weapons.

You can find all available SWEP fields here: [Structures/SWEP](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures/SWEP)

entries.name: WEAPON_PROFICIENCY
entries.description:
Enumerations used by [NPC:SetCurrentWeaponProficiency](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/NPC:SetCurrentWeaponProficiency) and  
[NPC:GetCurrentWeaponProficiency](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/NPC:GetCurrentWeaponProficiency).

items.description: The NPC will miss a large majority of their shots.
The NPC will miss about half of their shots.
The NPC will sometimes miss their shots.
The NPC will rarely miss their shots.
The NPC will almost never miss their shots.

entries.name: AcceptInput
entries.description: Called when another entity fires an event to this entity.

args.name: inputName
args.description: The name of the input that was triggered.

args.name: activator
args.description: The initial cause for the input getting triggered.

args.name: called
args.description: The entity that directly trigger the input.

args.name: data
args.description: The data passed.

returns.description: Should we suppress the default action for this input?

entries.name: AdjustMouseSensitivity
entries.description: Allows you to adjust the weapon's mouse sensitivity. This hook only works if you haven't overridden [GM:AdjustMouseSensitivity](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:AdjustMouseSensitivity).

args.name: defaultSensitivity
args.description:
The old sensitivity

In general this will be 0, which is equivalent to a sensitivity of 1.

args.name: localFOV
args.description: The player's current FOV.

args.name: defaultFOV
args.description: The player's default FOV.

returns.description: A multiplier of the player's normal sensitivity (0.5 would be half as sensitive, 2 would be twice as sensitive).

entries.name: AllowsAutoSwitchFrom
entries.description: Returns whether the weapon allows to being switched from when a better ( [Weapon:GetWeight](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:GetWeight) ) weapon is being picked up.

returns.description: Whether the weapon allows to being switched from.

entries.name: AllowsAutoSwitchTo
entries.description: Returns whether the weapon allows to being switched to when a better ([Weapon:GetWeight](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:GetWeight)) weapon is being picked up.

returns.description: Whether the weapon allows to being switched to.

entries.name: Ammo1
entries.description: Returns how much of primary ammo the player has.

returns.description: The amount of primary ammo player has

entries.name: Ammo2
entries.description: Returns how much of secondary ammo the player has.

returns.description: The amount of secondary ammo player has

entries.name: CalcView
entries.description:
Allows you to adjust player view while this weapon in use.

This hook is called from the default implementation of [GM:CalcView](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:CalcView) which is [here](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/base/gamemode/cl_init.lua#L387-L395). Therefore, it will not be called if any other hook added to `CalcView` returns any value, or if the current gamemode overrides the default hook and does not call the SWEP function.

args.name: ply
args.description: The owner of weapon

args.name: pos
args.description: Current position of players view

args.name: ang

New angle of players view
New FOV of players view

args.name: OldEyeAng

args.name: EyePos
args.description: Current position

args.name: EyeAng

returns.description: New position
New angle

entries.name: CallOnClient
entries.description:
Calls a SWEP function on client. Does nothing on client.

**WARNING**: This uses the [usermessage](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/usermessage) internally, because of that, the combined length of the arguments of this function may not exceed 254 bytes/characters or the function will cease to function!

args.name: functionName
args.description: Name of function to call. If you want to call `SWEP:MyFunc()` on client, you type in `"MyFunc"`

args.name: data
args.description: Custom data to be passed to the target SWEP function as the first argument.

entries.name: CanBePickedUpByNPCs
entries.description: Called when a Citizen NPC is looking around to a (better) weapon to pickup.

returns.description: Return true to allow this weapon to be picked up by NPCs.

entries.name: CanPrimaryAttack
entries.description: Helper function for checking for no ammo.

returns.description: Can use primary attack

entries.name: CanSecondaryAttack
entries.description: Helper function for checking for no ammo.

returns.description: Can use secondary attack

entries.name: Clip1
entries.description:
Returns how much primary ammo is in the magazine.
	**NOTE**: This is not shared between clients and will instead return the maximum primary clip size.

returns.description: The amount of primary ammo in the magazine.

entries.name: Clip2
entries.description:
Returns how much secondary ammo is in the magazine.
	**NOTE**: This is not shared between clients and will instead return the maximum secondary clip size.

returns.description: The amount of secondary ammo in the magazine.

entries.name: CustomAmmoDisplay
entries.description:
Allows you to use any numbers you want for the ammo display on the HUD.

Can be useful for weapons that don't use standard ammo.

returns.description:
The new ammo display settings. A table with 4 possible keys: (All default to -1)
* boolean Draw - Whether to draw the ammo display or not
* number PrimaryClip - Amount of primary ammo in the clip
* number PrimaryAmmo - Amount of primary ammo in the reserves
* number SecondaryAmmo - Amount of secondary ammo. It is shown like alt-fire for SMG1 and AR2 are shown.
* number SecondaryClip - Amount of secondary ammo in the clip. If set, the secondary ammo display will have clips and reserve ammo dispalyed.

entries.name: DefaultReload
entries.description:
Forces the weapon to reload while playing given animation.
	**NOTE**: This will stop the [Weapon:Think](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:Think) function from getting called while the weapon is reloading!

args.name: act
args.description: Sequence to use as reload animation. Uses the Enums/ACT.

returns.description: Did reloading actually take place

entries.name: Deploy
entries.description:
Called when player has just switched to this weapon.

**NOTE**: Due to this hook being predicted, it is not called clientside in singleplayer at all, and in multiplayer it will not be called clientside if the weapon is switched with [Player:SelectWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SelectWeapon) or the "use" console command, however it will be called clientside with the default weapon selection menu and when using [CUserCmd:SelectWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/CUserCmd:SelectWeapon)

returns.description: Return true to allow switching away from this weapon using `lastinv` command

entries.name: DoDrawCrosshair
entries.description:
Called when the crosshair is about to get drawn, and allows you to override it.

This function will **not** be called if `SWEP.DrawCrosshair` is set to false or if player is affected by [Player:CrosshairDisable](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:CrosshairDisable).

args.name: x
args.description: X coordinate of the crosshair.

args.name: y
args.description: Y coordinate of the crosshair.

returns.description: Return true to override the default crosshair.

entries.name: DoImpactEffect
entries.description:
Called so the weapon can override the impact effects it makes.
**NOTE**: If the bullet was fired in a predicted environment, the hook will not be called on the `CLIENT` realm.

**NOTE**: This hook will also be called when `WEAPON:GetOwner():FireBullets` is called. While in `MULTIPLAYER`, this hook will be called on the respective state, but in `SINGLEPLAYER`, this hook will always be called on the `CLIENT` realm even if `FireBullets` was called on the `SERVER`.

args.name: tr
args.description: A Structures/TraceResult from player's eyes to the impact point

args.name: damageType
args.description: The damage type of bullet. See Enums/DMG

returns.description: Return true to not do the default thing - which is to call `UTIL_ImpactTrace` in C++

entries.name: DrawHUD
entries.description:
This hook allows you to draw on screen while this weapon is in use.

If you want to draw a custom crosshair, consider using [WEAPON:DoDrawCrosshair](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DoDrawCrosshair) instead.

entries.name: DrawHUDBackground
entries.description: This hook allows you to draw on screen while this weapon is in use. This hook is called **before** [WEAPON:DrawHUD](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawHUD) and is equivalent of [GM:HUDPaintBackground](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:HUDPaintBackground).

entries.name: DrawWeaponSelection
entries.description: This hook draws the selection icon in the weapon selection menu.

args.name: x
args.description: X coordinate of the selection panel

args.name: y
args.description: Y coordinate of the selection panel

args.name: width
args.description: Width of the selection panel

args.name: height
args.description: Height of the selection panel

args.name: alpha
args.description: Alpha value of the selection panel

entries.name: DrawWorldModel
entries.description:
Called when we are about to draw the opaque parts of the weapon's world model.

See [WEAPON:DrawWorldModelTranslucent](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawWorldModelTranslucent) for translucent pass callback.
See [WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn) for view model rendering.

args.name: flags
args.description: The Enums/STUDIO flags for this render operation.

entries.name: DrawWorldModelTranslucent
entries.description:
Called when we are about to draw the translucent parts of the weapon's world model.

See [WEAPON:DrawWorldModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawWorldModel) for opaque pass callback.
See [WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn) for view model rendering.

args.name: flags
args.description: The Enums/STUDIO flags for this render operation.

entries.name: Equip
entries.description: Called when a player or NPC has picked the weapon up.

args.name: NewOwner
args.description: The one who picked the weapon up. Can be Player or NPC.

entries.name: EquipAmmo
entries.description:
The player has picked up the weapon and has taken the ammo from it.
The weapon will be removed immediately after this call.

args.name: ply
args.description: The player who picked up the weapon

entries.name: FireAnimationEvent
entries.description:
Called before executing an animation event, such as a muzzle flash appearing or a shell ejecting.

This will only be called serverside for 3000-range events, and clientside for 5000-range and other events.

args.name: pos
args.description: Position of the effect.

args.name: ang
args.description: Angle of the effect.

args.name: event
args.description: The event ID of the happened event. See [this page](http://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Animation_Events).

args.name: options
args.description: Name or options of the event.

args.name: source
args.description: The source entity. This will be a viewmodel on the client and the weapon itself on the server

returns.description: Return true to disable the effect.

entries.name: FreezeMovement
entries.description:
This hook allows you to freeze players screen.
**NOTE**: Player will still be able to move or shoot

returns.description: Return true to freeze moving the view

entries.name: GetActivity
entries.description:
Returns the sequence enumeration number that the weapon is playing.

This can return inconsistent results between the server and client.

returns.description: Current activity, see Enums/ACT. Returns 0 if the weapon doesn't have active sequence.

entries.name: GetCapabilities
entries.description:
This hook is for NPCs, you return what they should try to do with it.
	**WARNING**: Calling [NPC:CapabilitiesGet](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/NPC:CapabilitiesGet) in this hook on the same entity can cause infinite loops since that function adds the result of [WEAPON:GetCapabilities](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:GetCapabilities) on top of the return value.

returns.description: A number defining what NPC should do with the weapon. Use the Enums/CAP.

entries.name: GetDeploySpeed
entries.description: Returns the weapon deploy speed, as set by [Weapon:SetDeploySpeed](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:SetDeploySpeed). If not previously set, the value will be polled from the `sv_defaultdeployspeed` [ConVar](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ConVar).

returns.name: speed

entries.name: GetHoldType
entries.description: Returns the hold type of the weapon.

entries.name: GetMaxClip1
entries.description: Returns maximum primary clip size

returns.description: Maximum primary clip size

returns.description: Maximum secondary clip size

returns.description: The time, relative to Global.CurTime

entries.name: GetNextSecondaryFire
entries.description: Gets the next time the weapon can secondary fire. ( Can call [WEAPON:SecondaryAttack](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:SecondaryAttack) )

returns.description: The time, relative to Global.CurTime

entries.name: GetNPCBulletSpread
entries.description:
Called when the weapon is used by NPCs to determine how accurate the bullets fired should be.

The inaccuracy is simulated by changing the [NPC:GetAimVector](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/NPC:GetAimVector) based on the value returned from this hook.

args.description: How proficient the NPC is with this gun. See Enums/WEAPON_PROFICIENCY

returns.description: Minimum amount of time the NPC can rest (not shoot) between bursts in seconds. Default is `0.3` seconds.
Maximum amount of time the NPC can rest (not shoot) between bursts in seconds. Default is `0.6` seconds.

Returns the non-internal name of the weapon, that should be for displaying.

entries.name: Holster
entries.description:
Called when weapon tries to holster.

**NOTE**: This will only be called serverside when using [Player:SelectWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:SelectWeapon) as that function immediately switches the weapon out of prediction.


This is called twice for every holster clientside, one in [Prediction](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Prediction) and one not.

Before [WEAPON:OnRemove](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:OnRemove) is called, this function is only called serverside.

args.name: weapon
args.description: The weapon we are trying switch to.

returns.description:
Return true to allow weapon to holster.

This will not have an effect if weapon was switched away from using Player:SetActiveWeapon

entries.name: HUDShouldDraw
entries.description: This hook determines which parts of the HUD to draw.

args.name: element
args.description: The HUD element in question

returns.description: Return false to hide this HUD element

entries.name: Initialize
entries.description:
Called when the weapon entity is created.

**NOTE**: [Entity:GetOwner](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetOwner) will return NULL at this point because the weapon is not equpped by a player or NPC yet. Use [WEAPON:Equip](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:Equip) or [WEAPON:Deploy](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:Deploy) if you need the owner to be valid.


This is not called serverside after a quicksave.

entries.name: IsScripted
entries.description: Checks if the weapon is a SWEP or a built-in weapon.

returns.description: Returns true if weapon is scripted ( SWEP ), false if not ( A built-in HL2/HL:S weapon )

entries.description: Returns whether the weapon is visible. The term visibility is not exactly what gets checked here, first it checks if the owner is a player, then checks if the active view model has EF_NODRAW flag NOT set.

entries.name: KeyValue
entries.description:
Called when the engine sets a value for this scripted weapon.

See [GM:EntityKeyValue](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:EntityKeyValue) for a hook that works for all entities.


See [ENTITY:KeyValue](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ENTITY:KeyValue) for an  hook that works for scripted entities.

args.name: key

args.description: The new value.

entries.name: LastShootTime

returns.description: The time in seconds when the last bullet was fired.

entries.name: NPCShoot_Primary
entries.description:
Called internally during `TASK_RANGE_ATTACK1 --> OnRangeAttack1`. This allows you to separate your SWEPs primary firing function from players and NPCs. 

To get the delay the NPC will fire again, you can call `self:GetOwner():GetInternalVariable("m_flNextAttack")`

**NOTE**: This hook is called internally only for NPCs that has `CAP_USE_SHOT_REGULATOR` set.

args.name: shootPos
args.description: The world position the NPC will use as attack starting position. You can create your projectiles here.

args.name: shootDir
args.description: The direction the NPC wants to shoot at.

entries.name: NPCShoot_Secondary
entries.description:
A utility function to seperate your SWEPs secondary firing from players. 

Unlike [WEAPON:NPCShoot_Primary](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:NPCShoot_Primary), this won't be called by the engine for `TASK_RANGE_ATTACK2`.

args.name: shootPos
args.description: The world position the NPC will use as attack starting position. You can create your projectiles here.

args.name: shootDir
args.description: The direction the NPC wants to shoot at.

entries.name: OnDrop
entries.description:
Called when weapon is dropped by [Player:DropWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:DropWeapon).

See also [WEAPON:OwnerChanged](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:OwnerChanged).

args.name: owner
args.description: The entity that dropped the weapon.

entries.name: OnReloaded
entries.description: Called whenever the weapons Lua script is reloaded.

entries.name: OnRemove
entries.description:
Called when the [Scripted Weapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Scripted_Entities) is about to be removed.

[Entity:GetOwner](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:GetOwner) may be unset at this point, see [WEAPON:OnDrop](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:OnDrop) and [WEAPON:OwnerChanged](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:OwnerChanged).

entries.name: OnRestore
entries.description:
Called when the weapon entity is reloaded from a Source Engine save (not the Sandbox saves or dupes) or on a changelevel (for example Half-Life 2 campaign level transitions).

For the [duplicator](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/duplicator) callbacks, see [ENTITY:OnDuplicated](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/ENTITY:OnDuplicated).

See also [saverestore](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/saverestore) for relevant functions.

entries.name: OwnerChanged
entries.description:
Called when weapon is dropped or picked up by a new player. This can be called clientside for all players on the server if the weapon has no owner and is picked up.

See also [WEAPON:OnDrop](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:OnDrop).

entries.name: PostDrawViewModel
entries.description:
Called after the view model has been drawn while the weapon in use.

This hook relies on default implementation of [GM:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PostDrawViewModel). If it appears to not work, it may have been overwritten/broken by the currently active gamemode or other addons.

[WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn) is an alternative hook which is always called before [GM:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PostDrawViewModel).

See also [WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel).

args.name: vm
args.description: This is the view model entity after it is drawn

args.name: weapon
args.description: This is the weapon that is from the view model (same as self)

args.name: ply
args.description: The owner of the view model

args.name: flags
args.description: The Enums/STUDIO flags for this render operation.

entries.name: PreDrawViewModel
entries.description:
Allows you to modify viewmodel while the weapon in use before it is drawn.

This hook relies on default implementation of [GM:PreDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PreDrawViewModel). If it appears to not work, it may have been overwritten/broken by the currently active gamemode or other addons.

See also [WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn) and [WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel).

args.name: vm
args.description: This is the view model entity before it is drawn.

args.name: weapon
args.description: This is the weapon that is from the view model.

args.name: ply
args.description: The the owner of the view model.

args.name: flags
args.description: The Enums/STUDIO flags for this render operation.

returns.description: Return `true` to prevent the default action of rendering the view model. `PostDrawViewModel` will NOT be called in this scenario.

entries.name: PrimaryAttack
entries.description:
Called when primary attack button ( +attack ) is pressed.

When in singleplayer, this function is only called in the server realm. When in multiplayer, the hook will be called on both the server and the client in order to allow for [Prediction](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Prediction).

You can force the hook to always be called on client like this:

```
if ( game.SinglePlayer() ) then self:CallOnClient( "PrimaryAttack" ) end
```


Note that due to prediction, in multiplayer SWEP:PrimaryAttack is called multiple times per one "shot" with the gun. To work around that, use [Global.IsFirstTimePredicted](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.IsFirstTimePredicted).

entries.name: PrintWeaponInfo
entries.description: A convenience function that draws the weapon info box, used in [WEAPON:DrawWeaponSelection](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawWeaponSelection).

args.name: x
args.description: The x co-ordinate of box position

args.name: y
args.description: The y co-ordinate of box position

args.name: alpha
args.description: Alpha value for the box

entries.name: Reload
entries.description: Called when the reload key ( +reload ) is pressed.

entries.name: RenderScreen
entries.description:
Called every frame just before [GM:RenderScene](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:RenderScene).

Used by the Tool Gun to render view model screens ([TOOL:DrawToolScreen](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/TOOL:DrawToolScreen)).


**NOTE**: Materials rendered in this hook require $ignorez parameter to draw properly.

entries.name: SecondaryAttack
entries.description:
Called when secondary attack button ( +attack2 ) is pressed.

For issues with this hook being called rapidly on the client side, see the global function [Global.IsFirstTimePredicted](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.IsFirstTimePredicted).

args.description: Activity to play. See the Enums/ACT (specifically `ACT_VM_`).

Sets the activity the weapon is playing.

See also [Weapon:GetActivity](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:GetActivity).

args.name: act
args.description: The new activity to set, see Enums/ACT.

entries.description: Sets the weapon deploy speed. This value needs to match on client and server.

args.name: speed
args.description: The value to set deploy speed to. Values less than `1` will slow down the animations. Minimum value is `0.1`.

entries.name: SetHoldType
entries.description:
Sets the hold type of the weapon. This function also calls [WEAPON:SetWeaponHoldType](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:SetWeaponHoldType) and properly networks it to all clients.

**NOTE**: This only works on scripted weapons.


Using this function on weapons held by bots will not network holdtype changes to clients if the world model is set to an empty string (SWEP.WorldModel = "").

args.name: name
args.description: Name of the hold type. You can find all default hold types Hold_Types

entries.name: SetLastShootTime
entries.description:
Sets the time since this weapon last fired in seconds. Used in conjunction with [Weapon:LastShootTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:LastShootTime).

This value is **not** networked to the client if set from server.

args.name: time
args.description: The time in seconds when the last time the weapon was fired.

entries.name: SetNextPrimaryFire
entries.description:
Sets when the weapon can fire again. Time should be based on [Global.CurTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CurTime).

**NOTE**: The standard HL2 Pistol (`weapon_pistol`) bypasses this function due to an [internal implementation](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/hl2/weapon_pistol.cpp#L313-L317).

This will fire extra bullets if the time is set to less than [Global.CurTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CurTime).

args.name: time
args.description: Time when player should be able to use primary fire again

entries.name: SetNextSecondaryFire
entries.description: Sets when the weapon can alt-fire again. Time should be based on [Global.CurTime](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.CurTime).

args.name: time
args.description: Time when player should be able to use secondary fire again

entries.name: SetupDataTables
entries.description: Called when the SWEP should set up its [ Data Tables](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Networking_Entities).

entries.name: SetWeaponHoldType
entries.description:
Sets the hold type of the weapon. This must be called on **both** the server and the client to work properly.

**NOTE**: You should avoid calling this function and call [Weapon:SetHoldType](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:SetHoldType) now.

Should this weapon be dropped when its owner dies?

This only works if the player has [Player:ShouldDropWeapon](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:ShouldDropWeapon) set to true.

entries.name: Think
entries.description:
Called when the weapon thinks.

This hook won't be called during the deploy animation and when using [Weapon:DefaultReload](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:DefaultReload). 

**NOTE**: If you wish for this hook to be called during the deploy animation, add the following to the model's **ACT_VM_DRAW** sequence: `node "Ready"`


Despite being a predicted hook, this hook is called clientside in single player (for your convenience), however it will not be recognized as a predicted hook via [Player:GetCurrentCommand](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player:GetCurrentCommand), and will run more often in this case.

This hook will be called before Player movement is processed on the client, and after on the server.

**NOTE**: This hook only runs while the weapon is in players hands. It does not run while it is carried by an NPC.

This will not be run during deploy animations after a serverside-only deploy. This usually happens after picking up and dropping an object with +use.

entries.name: Tick
entries.description: Alias of [Weapon:Think](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Weapon:Think).
entries.deprecated: Use Weapon:Think instead.

entries.name: TranslateActivity
entries.description:
Translate a generic activity into a more specific activity, such as holdtype-specific activities.

The translated activity is then used to request animations from the owner's model via [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence) and similar functions.

For example, `ACT_MP_RUN` becomes `ACT_HL2MP_RUN_PISTOL`.

args.name: act
args.description: The activity to translate

returns.name: act
returns.description: The translated activity

entries.name: TranslateFOV
entries.description:
Allows to change players field of view while player holds the weapon.

**NOTE**: This hook must be defined shared and return same value on both to properly affect Area Portals.

args.name: fov
args.description: The current/default FOV.

returns.description: The target FOV.

entries.name: ViewModelDrawn

Called straight after the view model has been drawn. This is called before [GM:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/GM:PostDrawViewModel) and [WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel).

See [WEAPON:DrawWorldModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:DrawWorldModel) for world model rendering.

See also [WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel) and [WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel).

args.name: ViewModel
args.description: Players view model

args.name: flags
args.description: The Enums/STUDIO flags for this render operation.

entries.name: weapons
entries.description: The weapons library allows you to access information about any scripted weapons loaded into the game, as well as register your own weapons.

entries.name: Get
entries.description:
Get a `copy` of weapon table by name. This function also inherits fields from the weapon's base class, unlike [weapons.GetStored](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.GetStored) or [weapons.GetList](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.GetList).
	**NOTE**: This will only work on SWEP's, this means that this will not return anything for HL2/HL:S weapons.

args.name: classname
args.description: Class name of weapon to retrieve

returns.description: The retrieved table or nil

entries.name: GetList
entries.description:
Get a list of all the registered SWEPs. This does not include weapons added to spawnmenu manually.
	**NOTE**: This function does not inherit fields from the weapon's base class, unlike [weapons.Get](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.Get)

returns.description: List of all the registered SWEPs

entries.name: GetStored
entries.description:
Gets the REAL weapon table, not a copy. The produced table does *not* inherit fields from the weapon's base class, unlike [weapons.Get](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.Get).

**WARNING**: Modifying this table will modify what is stored by the weapons library. Take a copy or use [weapons.Get](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.Get) to avoid this.

args.name: weapon_class
args.description: Weapon class to retrieve weapon table of

returns.description: The weapon table

entries.name: IsBasedOn
entries.description: Checks if name is based on base

args.name: name
args.description: Entity's class name to be checked

args.name: base
args.description: Base class name to be checked

returns.description: Returns true if class name is based on base, else false.

entries.name: OnLoaded
entries.description:
**INTERNAL**: This is used internally - although you're able to use it you probably shouldn't.


Called after all SWEPS have been loaded and runs [baseclass.Set](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/baseclass.Set) on each one.

You can retrieve all the currently registered SWEPS with [weapons.GetList](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.GetList).

**NOTE**: This is not called after a SWEP auto refresh, and thus the inherited baseclass functions retrieved with [baseclass.Get](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/baseclass.Get) will not be updated

entries.name: Register
entries.description:
Registers a Scripted Weapon (SWEP) class manually. When the engine spawns an entity, weapons registered with this function will be created if the class names match.

See also [scripted_ents.Register](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/scripted_ents.Register) for Scripted Entities (SENTs)

Sub-tables provided in the first argument will not carry over their metatable, and will receive a BaseClass key if the table was merged with the base's. Userdata references, which includes Vectors, Angles, Entities, etc. will not be copied.

args.name: SWEP
args.description:
The SWEP table to register.  
			For the table's format and available options see the Structures/SWEP page.

args.name: classname
args.description: Classname to assign to that swep

entries.name: widgets

The widgets library.

Widgets allow the player to have mouse interaction with entities, such as being able to manipulate the [bones of an NPC](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O3gG0t39-pQ).

entries.name: WorkshopFileBase

**INTERNAL**: This is used internally - although you're able to use it you probably shouldn't.

		This object is created by [Global.WorkshopFileBase](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.WorkshopFileBase) which is used internally to fetch data of the specific namespace

		**NOTE**: You need to set the `HTML` field to a [DHTML](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/DHTML) panel that is set up correctly like [here](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/sandbox/gamemode/spawnmenu/creationmenu/content/contenttypes/dupes.lua#L12), or else you might get errors.
